nodes.name: Residue fields of fibers of a good-reduction morphism (local)
nodes.statement:
Let \(\psi\colon C \to D\) be a morphism of smooth projective geometrically integral curves over a nonarchimedean local field \(K\) that has good reduction (so there is an integral model \(\Psi\colon {\mathcal C} \to {\mathcal D}\); see Definition~\ref{def:GoodReductionOfCurves}), let \(t\in D(K)\) be outside the branch locus of \(\psi\), let \(\overline{t}\in {\mathcal D}({\mathbb F}_K)\) be the specialization of \(t\), and let \(\overline{x}\in {\mathcal C}_{\overline{t}}\).
    Then every maximal subfield \(L\subset{\mathbf k}(C_{t})_{\overline{x}}\) has the following numerical invariants.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The inertia degree \(f(L/K)\) is divisible by the degree of \(\overline{x}\).
        \item The ramification index \(e(L/K)\) divides the ramification index \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\) of the morphism \(\Psi_{{\mathbb F}_K}\) at the point \(\overline{x}\).
        \item If \(e(L/K)=e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\) (i.e., the ramification index \(e(L/k)\) is as large as possible), then \(L = {\mathbf k}(C_{t})_{\overline{x}}\) and the inertia degree is \(f(L/K)=\deg(\overline{x})\).        
    \end{enumerate}
    Conversely, every extension \(L/K\) with ramification degree \(e:= e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\) and inertia degree \(f:=\deg(\overline{x})\) is isomorphic to \({\mathbf k}(C_{t})_{\overline{x}}\) for some \(t\in {\mathcal D}(K)\) specializing to \(\overline{t}\) \emph{if and only if} 
    \[
        \gcd\left(e, \frac{q^f - 1}{q-1}\right) = 1 \quad \mbox{where }q := \#{\mathbb F}_K.
    \]
nodes.statement_short: For a good-reduction cover over a local field, inertia degree divisible by deg(x̄), ramification divides e(x̄/t̄); every (e,f) extension is realized iff gcd(e,(q^f-1)/(q-1))=1.

nodes.name: Proportion of realizable extensions
nodes.statement: In the case that \(\gcd\left(e, \frac{q^f - 1}{q-1}\right)\neq 1\), the more general Theorem~\ref{thm:RamAndInertiaDegrees} describes which extensions \(L/K\) with fixed numerical invariants are realized as \({\mathbf k}(C_{t})_{\overline{x}}\) for some point \(t\). nodes.name: Comparison with Beckmann, Debes, Ghazi, Konig, Legrand, Neftin
nodes.statement: If \(\psi\) is a Galois cover or if \(D = {\mathbb P}^1\), then prior results of Beckmann, D\`ebes, Ghazi, K\"onig, Legrand, and Neftin essentially combine to give statements (1)--(3) from the theorem~\cites{Beckmann, DG2012, KLN-GrunwaldRamified, DL-TAMS, Legrand}. (Our notion of good reduction is not identical to the conditions that appear in these works but they differ up to a finite set of places.) If both assumptions hold (i.e., \(\psi\) is Galois and \(D= {\mathbb P}^1\), then~\cite{KLN-GrunwaldRamified} gives a group-theoretic characterization of the extensions \(L/K\) that appear as \({\mathbf k}(C_{t})_{\overline{x}}\) for some \(t\in {\mathbb P}^1(K)\). This group theoretic characterization is in terms of the relationship between the geometric inertia group of a ramification point embedded as a subgroup of \(\mathrm{Gal}(\psi)\) and the arithmetic inertia group \(\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K^{nr})\). See Section~\ref{sec:IntroComparison} for a comparison of the approaches.
nodes.statement_short: For Galois covers or D = P^1, prior work gives parts (1)-(3); for Galois covers of P^1, KLN give a group-theoretic characterization.

nodes.name: Residue fields of fibers of general degree d covers of P^1
nodes.statement_short: For degree d covers with ramification indices at most 2 and v with large residue field: every partition occurs as inertia degrees, ramification at most 2 and bounded, and quadratic ramified extensions occur.
assumptions: \(\psi \colon C \to {\mathbb P}^1\) be a degree \(d\) morphism of smooth projective geometrically integral curves such that all points of \(C\) have ramification index at most \(2\)
\(v\) be a nonarchimedean place of \(k\) with sufficiently large residue field
conclusions: For all partitions \((d_i)_{i=1}^r\vdash d\), there exists a \(t\in {\mathbb P}^1(k)\) such that \({\mathbf k}(C_t)\) is a field with \(r\) places \(w_i|v\), each of inertia degree \(f(w_i/v) = d_i\).
For every \(t\in {\mathbb P}^1(k)\) outside the branch locus and every place \(w|v\) of \({\mathbf k}(C_t)\), the ramification degree \(e(w/v)\) is at most \(2.\)

If \(\psi\) has a \(k_v\)-rational branch point and there is an odd degree ramification point \(x_v\in C\) lying above it, then for all quadratic ramified extensions \(L/{\mathbf k}(x_v)\), there exists a \(t\in {\mathbb P}^1(k)\) such that \({\mathbf k}(C_t)\otimes_k k_v\) contains \(L\) as a maximal subfield.
nodes.label: thm:SdIntro

nodes.name: Analogous results for fixed ramification data
nodes.statement: For any cover \(C\to {\mathbb P}^1\) whose combinatorial ramification data is fixed, we can obtain a result analogous to Theorem~\ref{thm:SdIntro}. Indeed, standard arguments involving spreading out, Hilbert irreducibility, and weak approximation (which we review in detail in Section~\ref{sec:Global}) reduce the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:SdIntro} (and results analogous to it) to studying possible isomorphism classes of \'etale \(k_v\)-algebras \({\mathbf k}(C_t)\) for \(t\in {\mathbb P}^1(k_v)\), which we may do using Theorem~\ref{thm:RamAndInertiaDegrees}.
nodes.statement_short: Spreading out, Hilbert irreducibility and weak approximation reduce Theorem 1.3-type results to local étale algebras, handled by Theorem 4.2.

nodes.name: Nonarchimedean local field K, valuation ring, residue field
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper, we use \(K\) to denote a nonarchimedean local field, \({\mathcal O}_K\) its valuation ring, and \({\mathbb F}_K\) its residue field.

nodes.name: Uniformizer and residue field size
nodes.statement: We let \(\pi_K\) denote a uniformizer and write \(q_K := \#{\mathbb F}_K\).

nodes.name: Maximal tamely ramified and unramified extensions
nodes.statement: We write \(K^{tr}\) for the maximal tamely ramified extension of \(K\) and \(K^{nr}\subset K^{tr}\) for the maximal unramified subextension.

nodes.name: Unramified extension K(d)
nodes.statement: Given any positive integer \(d\) and a local field \(K\), we write \(K(d)\) for the unique unramified degree \(d\) extension of \(K\).

nodes.name: Finite field extension F(d)
nodes.statement: Similarly, if \({\mathbb F}\) is a finite field, we write \({\mathbb F}({d})\) for the unique degree \({d}\) extension of \({\mathbb F}\).

nodes.name: Classification of étale extensions of O_K
nodes.statement: We will often use that any local \'etale extension of \({\mathcal O}_K\) is isomorphic to \({\mathcal O}_{K({d})}\) for some \({d}\) and this in turn implies that any (not necessarily local) \'etale extension of \({\mathcal O}_K\) is a product \(\prod_{d_i}{\mathcal O}_{K(d_i)}\) for some integers \(d_i\).
nodes.statement_short: Local étale extensions of O_K are O_{K(d)}; general étale extensions are products of these.
conclusions: any local \'etale extension of \({\mathcal O}_K\) is isomorphic to \({\mathcal O}_{K({d})}\) for some \({d}\)

nodes.name: Haar measure on O_K
nodes.statement: Since ${\mathcal O}_K$ is locally compact, it comes equipped with a Haar measure, which we denote by \(\mu_{{\mathcal O}_K}\).

nodes.name: Haar measure on subschemes of P^1
nodes.statement: Since \({\mathbb P}^1\) can be obtained by gluing together two copies of \({\mathbb A}^1\) and \({\mathbb A}^1({\mathcal O}_K) \simeq {\mathcal O}_K\), we can extend \(\mu_{{\mathcal O}_K}\) to a Haar measure \(\mu_V\) for \(V\) a reduced subscheme of \({\mathbb P}^1_{{\mathcal O}_K}\).

nodes.name: Specialization
nodes.statement: Given a proper \({\mathcal O}_K\) scheme \({\mathscr X} \to \mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_K\), and a closed point on the generic fiber \(x\in {\mathscr X}_K\), the valuative criterion of properness allows us to extend to a map \(\mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_{{\mathbf k}(x)}\to {\mathscr X}\). In particular, restricting this morphism to the unique closed point of \(\mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_{{\mathbf k}(x)}\) gives a closed point \(\overline{x}\in{\mathscr X}\). We say this point \(\overline{x}\) is the \defi{specialization} of \(x\) and write \(x\rightsquigarrow \overline{x}\) to indicate that \(x\) specializes to \(\overline{x}\).

nodes.name: Number field k and its places
nodes.statement: We reserve \(k\) for number fields, and denote the set of places of \(k\) by \(\Omega_k\).

nodes.name: Completion at a place
nodes.statement: Given a nonarchimedean \(v\in \Omega_k\), we write \(k_v\) for the completion and \({\mathcal O}_v, {\mathbb F}_v, \pi_v\) for its valuation ring, residue field, and a choice of uniformizer, respectively.

nodes.name: Norm map
nodes.statement: Given any finite extension of fields \(L/F\), we write \(N_{L/F}\colon L^{\times} \to F^{\times}\) for the norm map.

nodes.name: Ramification and inertia degrees of local fields
nodes.statement:
Given a finite extension of local fields \(L/K\), we write \(e(L/K)\) and \(f(L/K)\) for the ramification and inertia degrees, respectively. In other words,
    \[
        f(L/K) = [{\mathbb F}_L : {\mathbb F}_K]\quad \textup{and}\quad \pi_L^{e(L/K)}{\mathcal O}_L = \pi_K{\mathcal O}_L.
    \]

nodes.name: Ramification degree of local ring extension
nodes.statement: We also consider the ramification degree \(e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R)\) of a finite extension of local rings \((R, {\mathfrak m}_R) \hookrightarrow (S, {\mathfrak m}_S)\), which we define to be the ratio \(\dim_{R/{\mathfrak m}_R}(S/{\mathfrak m}_RS)/\dim_{R/{\mathfrak m}_R}(S/{\mathfrak m}_S)\).
nodes.statement_short: e(m_S/m_R) := dim of S/m_R S over the dim of the residue field extension.

nodes.name: Agreement with the usual ramification degree
nodes.statement: If \(R\) and \(S\) are discrete valuation rings and their extension of fraction fields is separable, then this agrees with the usual ramification degree which measures the index of value groups.

nodes.name: Closed subgroup generated by an element
nodes.statement: For a profinite group \(G\) and an element \(g\in G\), we write \(\langle g \rangle\) for the closed subgroup topologically generated by \(g\).

nodes.name: Cycle type
nodes.statement: For a finite subgroup \(G\) of \(S_d\), we may write every element \(g\in G\) as a product of disjoint cycles, so we define the \defi{cycle type} of \(g\), denoted \(\mathrm{ct}(g)\), to be the multiset of lengths of the disjoint cycles.
nodes.genus: the multiset of lengths of the disjoint cycles

nodes.name: Partition notation
nodes.statement: The cycle type always gives a partition of \(d\), which we denote \(\mathrm{ct}(g)\vdash d.\)

nodes.name: Associated divisor and ring k(Z)
nodes.statement:
Given a smooth proper scheme of finite type \(X\) and a codimension \(1\) subscheme \(Z\subset X\), we write \(D_Z := \sum_{D\subset Z} n_D(Z) D\)
    be the associated effective divisor on \(X\), where \(D\) runs through the irreducible components of \(Z\), and we write \({\mathbf k}(Z)\) for the 
    ring
    \[
    {\mathbf k}(Z) = {\mathbf k}(D_Z) := \prod_{D} {\mathcal O}_{X,D}/{\mathfrak m}_D^{n_D(Z)}.
    \]
nodes.statement_short: D_Z is the effective divisor of a codimension 1 subscheme Z and k(Z) is the product of the local rings O_{X,D}/m_D^{n_D(Z)}.

nodes.name: k(Z) for integral and reduced Z
nodes.statement: Note that if \(Z\) is integral, then \({\mathbf k}(Z)\) is the residue field of \(Z\) and if \(Z\) is reduced, then \({\mathbf k}(Z)\) is the ring of global sections of the sheaf of total quotient rings.

nodes.name: Correspondence between function fields and normal projective curves
nodes.statement: Recall that for any field \(F\), there is a bijection between field extensions \(L/F\) of transcendence degree \(1\) and normal projective curves \(C/F\)~\cite{QingLiu}*{Proposition 7.3.13}.
assumptions: for any field \(F\)
conclusions: there is a bijection between field extensions \(L/F\) of transcendence degree \(1\) and normal projective curves \(C/F\)

nodes.name: Galois morphism
nodes.statement: For example, given a separable morphism \(\psi\colon C \to {\mathbb P}^1\) of normal projective curves, we say that the \(\psi\) is Galois if the corresponding extension of function fields is Galois.

nodes.name: Galois closure of a morphism
nodes.statement: Further, the Galois closure of \(\psi\) is a morphism of normal projective curves \(\widehat \psi \colon \widehat C \to {\mathbb P}^1\) such that the extension of function fields from \(\widehat\psi\) is the Galois closure of the map of function fields given by \(\psi\).

nodes.name: Galois groups of covers
nodes.statement: We also write \(\mathrm{Gal}(\widehat{C}/{\mathbb P}^1)\) and \(\mathrm{Gal}(\widehat{C}/C)\) to mean the Galois groups of the function field extensions.

nodes.name: Isomorphism classes of totally tamely ramified extensions
nodes.statement:
Let $K$ be a nonarchimedean local field, let $L_1,L_2$ be totally tamely ramified extensions of $K$, and for \(i=1,2\), let \(K\subset F_i \subset L_i\) be the maximal subextensions that are abelian over \(K\).
    
    If \([L_1:K] = [L_2:K]\), then the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $L_1 = \sigma(L_2)$ for some \(\sigma\in \mathrm{Gal}({\overline{K}}/K)\). 
        \item \(F_1 = F_2\). 
        \item \(N_{F_1/K}(F_1^{\times}) = N_{F_2/K}(F_2^{\times})\).
        \item $N_{L_1/K}(L_1^{\times}) = N_{L_2/K}(L_2^{\times})$.
        \item For any choice of uniformizers \(\pi_i\in N_{F_i/K}(F_i^{\times})\), the ratio \(\pi_1/\pi_2\in {\mathcal O}_{K}^{\times [F_1:K]}\).
        \item For any choice of uniformizers \(\pi_i\in N_{L_i/K}(L_i^{\times})\), the ratio \(\pi_1/\pi_2\in {\mathcal O}_{K}^{\times [F_1:K]}\). 
        \item For any choice of uniformizers \(\pi_i\in N_{L_i/K}(L_i^{\times})\), the ratio \(\pi_1/\pi_2\in {\mathcal O}_{K}^{\times [L_1:K]}\). 
    \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For totally tamely ramified L1, L2 of equal degree: conjugacy is equivalent to equality of maximal abelian subextensions, of norm groups, and to uniformizer ratios being suitable powers.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.1
nodes.statement:
We are mainly interested in the equivalence of~\eqref{it:Conj} and~\eqref{it:UniformizerTTRam}. However, the tools which allow us to relate these two statements naturally give us the equivalent statements~\eqref{it:AbelianEqual}--\eqref{it:UniformizerTTRamModified}, as we now explain.
The equivalence of~\eqref{it:AbelianEqual} and~\eqref{it:NormAbelian} is a special case of the Main Theorem of Local Class Field Theory (abelian extensions are characterized by their norm groups); see, e.g., \cite{Neukirch}*{Chapter~V, Theorem~1.4}. Furthermore, using the local reciprocity map, we can deduce $N_{F_i/K}(F_i^{\times})\cap {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}={\mathcal O}_K^{\times [F_i:K]}$ which yields the equivalence of~\eqref{it:NormAbelian} and~\eqref{it:UniformizerAbelian}. The Norm Limitation Theorem~\cite{Grant-Leitzel}*{Theorem A} implies that \(N_{F_i/K}(F_i^{\times}) = N_{L_i/K}(L_i^{\times})\) which yields the equivalences~\eqref{it:NormAbelian}\(\Leftrightarrow\)\eqref{it:NormTTRam} and~\eqref{it:UniformizerAbelian}\(\Leftrightarrow\)\eqref{it:UniformizerTTRamModified}. Therefore, we have ascertained all equivalences among~\eqref{it:AbelianEqual}--\eqref{it:UniformizerTTRamModified}. Additionally, the implication~\eqref{it:Conj}\(\Rightarrow\)\eqref{it:AbelianEqual} follows from the Galois theory correspondence. It remains to prove ~\eqref{it:AbelianEqual}\(\Rightarrow\)\eqref{it:Conj} and~\eqref{it:UniformizerTTRamModified}\(\Leftrightarrow\)\eqref{it:UniformizerTTRam}.

The implication~\eqref{it:AbelianEqual}\(\Rightarrow\)\eqref{it:Conj} is proved in Corollary~\ref{cor:GaloisTotallyTamelyRamified}\eqref{part:conj}, which uses Iwasawa's presentation of \(\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K)\). Finally, Iwasawa's presentation of the Galois group also implies that \([F_i:K] = \gcd([L_i:K], q_K-1)\) (Corollary~\ref{cor:GaloisTotallyTamelyRamified}\eqref{part:index}) so \({\mathcal O}_K^{\times [L_1:K]} = {\mathcal O}_K^{\times \gcd([L_1:K], q_K-1)} = {\mathcal O}_K^{\times [F_1:K]}\) and this gives the equivalence of \eqref{it:UniformizerTTRamModified} and~\eqref{it:UniformizerTTRam}.
nodes.statement_short: Chain equivalences via the main theorem of local class field theory, the norm limitation theorem, and Corollary 2.6 from Iwasawa's presentation.

nodes.name: Iwasawa's presentation of the tame Galois group
nodes.statement:
Let \(K\) be a nonarchimedean local field.
The Galois group \(\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K^{nr})\) is isomorphic to {\(\prod_{p\nmid q_K} {\mathbb Z}_p\)} and the quotient \(\mathrm{Gal}(K^{nr}/K)\simeq \mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K)/\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K^{nr})\) is isomorphic to \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}\). Moreover, there is a generator \(\tau\) of \(\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K^{nr})\) and an element \(\sigma\in \mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K)\) whose image generates the quotient \(\mathrm{Gal}(K^{nr}/K)\) such that 
    \[
        \mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K) = \langle \tau, \sigma \,|\, \sigma\tau\sigma^{-1} = \tau^{q_K}\rangle.
    \]
nodes.statement_short: Gal(K^tr/K) is topologically generated by τ, σ with σ τ σ^{-1} = τ^q.
assumptions: \(K\) be a nonarchimedean local field
conclusions: The Galois group \(\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K^{nr})\) is isomorphic to {\(\prod_{p\nmid q_K} {\mathbb Z}_p\)}
\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K) = \langle \tau, \sigma \,|\, \sigma\tau\sigma^{-1} = \tau^{q_K}\rangle.
nodes.label: thm:Iwasawa

        \left|\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K)/\langle\tau\rangle H\right| = f(L/K).
    \]
    If \(L/K\) is totally tamely ramified, then \(H = \langle \tau^{e(L/K)}, \tau^i\sigma\rangle\) for some \(0 \leq i < e(L/K)\).
nodes.statement_short: For tame L/K, Gal(K^tr/L) meets <τ> in <τ^e> with index f; for totally tamely ramified L it is <τ^e, τ^iσ>.

nodes.name: Conjugacy of subgroups of the profinite metacyclic group
nodes.statement:
Let \(q\) be a prime power and let \({\mathcal G}\) be the profinite group generated by two elements \(\sigma, \tau\) with the only relation   
    \begin{equation} \sigma \tau \sigma^{-1} = \tau^q.
    \end{equation}
    Let \(e\) be a positive integer that is coprime to \(q\).
    For integers \(0\leq i < e\), define \(H_i := \langle \tau^e, \tau^i\sigma\rangle\).  Then \(H_i\) is conjugate to \(H_j\) if and only if \(i \equiv j \pmod{\gcd(e, q-1)}\).
nodes.statement_short: In the profinite group with σ τ σ^{-1} = τ^q, H_i = <τ^e, τ^iσ> and H_j are conjugate iff i ≡ j mod gcd(e, q-1).
assumptions: \(q\) be a prime power
\(e\) be a positive integer that is coprime to \(q\)
conclusions: \(H_i\) is conjugate to \(H_j\) if and only if \(i \equiv j \pmod{\gcd(e, q-1)}\)
nodes.label: lem:ProfiniteMetacyclic

nodes.name: Iwasawa relation
nodes.statement: \sigma \tau \sigma^{-1} = \tau^q.
nodes.label: eq:Iwasawa

nodes.name: Normality of <τ^i>
nodes.statement: Note that by~\eqref{eq:Iwasawa}, \(\langle \tau^i\rangle\) is a normal subgroup of \({\mathcal G}\) for all \(i\), and thus that \(\langle \tau^{qi}\rangle = \langle \tau^i\rangle\) for all \(i\).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement:
For a fixed \(i\), we compute that \(\tau^{-1}\tau^{i}\sigma\tau = \tau^{i + q-1}\sigma\). Thus, \(H_i\) is conjugate to \(H_{i + (q-1)\bmod e}\). By iterating, we deduce that \(H_i\) is conjugate to \(H_j\) if \(i \equiv j \pmod{\gcd(e, q-1)}\). Since \({\mathcal G}\) is generated by \(\sigma\) and \(\tau\), it suffices to show that if \(\sigma H_i\sigma^{-1} = H_j\) then \(i\equiv j \pmod{\gcd(e, q-1)}\). We compute 
    \[
    \sigma H_i\sigma^{-1} = \langle\sigma\tau^e\sigma^{-1}, \sigma\tau^i\sigma \sigma^{-1}\rangle = \langle \tau^{qe}, \tau^{qi}\sigma\rangle = \langle \tau^{e}, \tau^{qi}\sigma\rangle = H_{qi\bmod e}.
    \]
    This completes the proof, since \(qi = i + (q-1)i\equiv i \pmod{q-1}\).
nodes.statement_short: Conjugation by τ shifts i by q-1 and conjugation by σ multiplies i by q; both preserve i mod gcd(e,q-1).

nodes.name: Conjugating by τ sends H_i to H_{i+q-1}
nodes.statement: For a fixed \(i\), we compute that \(\tau^{-1}\tau^{i}\sigma\tau = \tau^{i + q-1}\sigma\). Thus, \(H_i\) is conjugate to \(H_{i + (q-1)\bmod e}\).
nodes.statement_short: Conjugating by τ sends H_i to H_{i+q-1}.

nodes.name: Iterate: congruent indices give conjugate subgroups
nodes.statement: By iterating, we deduce that \(H_i\) is conjugate to \(H_j\) if \(i \equiv j \pmod{\gcd(e, q-1)}\).
nodes.statement_short: Iterate: congruent indices give conjugate subgroups.

nodes.name: Reduce converse to conjugation by σ
nodes.statement: Since \({\mathcal G}\) is generated by \(\sigma\) and \(\tau\), it suffices to show that if \(\sigma H_i\sigma^{-1} = H_j\) then \(i\equiv j \pmod{\gcd(e, q-1)}\).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce converse to conjugation by σ.

nodes.name: σ H_i σ^{-1} = H_{qi mod e} and qi ≡ i mod q-1
nodes.statement:
We compute 
    \[
    \sigma H_i\sigma^{-1} = \langle\sigma\tau^e\sigma^{-1}, \sigma\tau^i\sigma \sigma^{-1}\rangle = \langle \tau^{qe}, \tau^{qi}\sigma\rangle = \langle \tau^{e}, \tau^{qi}\sigma\rangle = H_{qi\bmod e}.
    \]
    This completes the proof, since \(qi = i + (q-1)i\equiv i \pmod{q-1}\).
nodes.statement_short: σ H_i σ^{-1} = H_{qi mod e} and qi ≡ i mod q-1.

nodes.name: Galois subextensions of totally tamely ramified extensions
nodes.statement_short: For totally tamely ramified L/K of degree e, the maximal Galois subextension F is cyclic of degree gcd(e,q-1), and extensions containing F are conjugate to L.
assumptions: \(K\) be a nonarchimedean local field
\(L/K\) be a totally tamely ramified degree \(e\) extension
\(K\subset F\subset L\) be the maximal Galois subextension contained in \(L\)
conclusions: \(\mathrm{Gal}(F/K)\) is cyclic
\( [F:K] = \gcd\left(e, q_K - 1\right),\)
if \(L'/K\) is a totally tamely ramified degree \(e\) extension that contains \(F\), then \(L' = g(L)\) for some \(g\in \mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K)\).
nodes.label: cor:GaloisTotallyTamelyRamified

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.6
nodes.statement:
The extension \(F/K\) is totally ramified and Galois, thus \(\mathrm{Gal}(F/K)\) is a quotient of the cyclic profinite group \(\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/K^{nr})\) and  hence \(\mathrm{Gal}(F/K)\) is cyclic.
    
    Let \(H := \mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/L)\). Then by Corollary~\ref{cor:Iwasawa}, \(H\) is generated by \(\tau^e\) and \(\tau^i\sigma\) for some \(0\leq i < e=[L:K]\). Thus, Lemma~\ref{lem:ProfiniteMetacyclic} implies that \(H\) is a normal subgroup if and only if \([L:K]\mid q_K - 1\). Applying the same argument to subextensions of \(L\) we deduce that \([F:K] = \gcd(e, q_K - 1)\). 

    To prove the last statement, it suffices to show there exists a \(g\in \mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/F)\) such that \(L' = g(L)\), thus we may replace \(K\) with \(F\) and \(e\) with \(e/\gcd(e, q_K - 1)\) which equals \([L:F]\). In particular, we may assume that \(L/K\) has no nontrivial Galois subextensions. By the previous statement, this implies that \(\gcd(e, q_K - 1) =1\), which by Lemma~\ref{lem:ProfiniteMetacyclic} implies that \(\langle\tau^e, \tau^i\sigma\rangle\) is conjugate to \(\langle \tau^e, \tau^j\sigma \rangle\) for all \(i,j\). By Corollary~\ref{cor:Iwasawa}, \(\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/L)\) and \(\mathrm{Gal}(K^{tr}/L')\) both have this form, so the Galois correspondence yields the desired isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Cyclicity from the cyclic inertia quotient; degree and conjugacy from Corollary 2.3 and Lemma 2.4 after reducing to K = F.

nodes.name: Monogenicity of finite extensions of DVRs
nodes.statement: Finite extensions of discrete valuation rings with separable residue fields are always monogenic.
assumptions: Finite extensions of discrete valuation rings with separable residue fields
conclusions: are always monogenic

nodes.name: Non-monogenic extension F[[√x,√y]] over F[[x,y]]
nodes.statement:
Monogenicity can fail, however, for higher dimensional regular local rings.  For example, \(F[[\sqrt{x}, \sqrt{y}]]\) cannot be generated by a single element over \(F[[x,y]]\).\footnote{
By Nakayama's lemma, it suffices to show that there is no power basis for \(F[[\sqrt{x}, \sqrt{y}]]/\langle x, y\rangle\), which we can do by showing that \(1,\beta, \beta^2, \beta^3\) are linearly dependent in \(F[[\sqrt{x}, \sqrt{y}]]/\langle x, y\rangle\) for any \(\beta = c_0 + c_1\sqrt{x} + c_2\sqrt{y} + c_3\sqrt{xy}\).} Informally, the issue in this example is that there is ramification along two different axes.
nodes.statement_short: F[[√x,√y]] is not monogenic over F[[x,y]]: ramification along two axes.

conclusions: \(F[[\sqrt{x}, \sqrt{y}]]\) cannot be generated by a single element over \(F[[x,y]]\)

nodes.name: Monogenicity of regular local ring extensions with a single source of ramification
nodes.statement:
Let \((R,{\mathfrak m}_R)\) be a regular local ring and let \((S,{\mathfrak m}_S)\) be a regular local finite extension of \(R\). If there exists a height \(1\) prime \({\mathfrak q}_0\subset S\) such that \(R/{\mathfrak q}_0\cap R \to S/{\mathfrak q}_0\) is \'etale,
        then \(S\) is monogenic over \(R\), i.e., there exists a \(\beta\in S\) such that \(R[\beta] = S\).
nodes.statement_short: A finite extension of regular local rings, étale along some height 1 prime of S, is monogenic.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement:
Since \(R\to S\) is \'etale and \(S\) is local, \({\mathfrak m}_R S = {\mathfrak m}_S\). Furthermore, \'etale maps are preserved under base change, so \(R/{\mathfrak m}_R \to S\otimes R/{\mathfrak m}_R = S/{\mathfrak m}_S\) is \'etale. Thus, \(S/{\mathfrak m}_S\) is a separable extension of \(R/{\mathfrak m}_R\) 
        so by the primitive element theorem 
        there exists a \(\beta_0\in S/{\mathfrak m}_S\) such that \(S/{\mathfrak m}_S = R/{\mathfrak m}_R[\beta_0]\) and whose minimal polynomial \(f_0(z)\in R/{\mathfrak m}_R[z]\) is separable. In particular, \(f'_0(\beta_0)\not\equiv 0 \bmod {\mathfrak m}_S\).  If \(\beta\in S\) is a lift of \(\beta_0\), then we have: 
        \[
        R[\beta]/{\mathfrak m}_R \simeq (R/{\mathfrak m}_R)[\beta\bmod {\mathfrak m}_R S] = (R/{\mathfrak m}_R)[\beta\bmod {\mathfrak m}_S] = (R/{\mathfrak m}_R)[\beta_0] = S/{\mathfrak m}_S = S/{\mathfrak m}_RS.
        \]
        Thus, by Nakayama's lemma, \(R[\beta] = S\).  If \(f(z)\in R[z]\) denotes the minimal polynomial of \(\beta\), then \(f'(\beta)\bmod {\mathfrak m}_S= f_0'(\beta_0)\neq 0\). Therefore \(f'(\beta)\notin {\mathfrak m}_S\) and hence is a unit.
nodes.statement_short: Lift a primitive element of the separable residue extension; Nakayama gives R[β] = S and separability gives f'(β) a unit.

nodes.statement: Since \(R\to S\) is \'etale and \(S\) is local, \({\mathfrak m}_R S = {\mathfrak m}_S\). Furthermore, \'etale maps are preserved under base change, so \(R/{\mathfrak m}_R \to S\otimes R/{\mathfrak m}_R = S/{\mathfrak m}_S\) is \'etale.
nodes.statement_short: m_R S = m_S and the residue extension is étale.

Thus, \(S/{\mathfrak m}_S\) is a separable extension of \(R/{\mathfrak m}_R\)

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement:
If \(R\to S\) is \'etale, then we apply Lemma~\ref{lem:FiniteEtaleIsLocallyMonogenic}. Henceforth we assume that \(R\to S\) is not \'etale and let \({\mathfrak p}_0 := {\mathfrak q}_0 \cap R \). 
        Denote $R_0:=R/{\mathfrak p}_0$, ${\mathfrak m}_{R_0}:={\mathfrak m}_R/{\mathfrak p}_0$, $S_0:=S/{\mathfrak p}_0$, and ${\mathfrak m}_{S_0}:={\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak p}_0$.
        By assumption, \(R_0  \to S_0\) is \'etale, so Lemma~\ref{lem:FiniteEtaleIsLocallyMonogenic} implies that there is \(\beta_0\in S_0\) such that \(R_0[\beta_0] = S_0\) and furthermore, that  \(f_0'(\beta_0) \in S_0^{\times}\) where \(f_0(x)\) denotes the minimal polynomial of \(\beta_0\). Moreover, since \(R_0\to S_0\) is \'etale, \({\mathfrak m}_{S_0} = {\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak q}_0 = {\mathfrak m}_{R_0} S_0 = ({\mathfrak m}_R/{\mathfrak p}_0)(S/{\mathfrak q}_0)\), i.e., \({\mathfrak m}_S = {\mathfrak q}_0 + {\mathfrak m}_RS \).

        Choose \(\beta\in S\) to be a lift of \(\beta_0\) and choose \(f_1(z)\in R[z]\) to be a monic lift of \(f_0\). Note that this implies that \(f_1\bmod {\mathfrak p}_0\) is the minimal polynomial of \(\beta\bmod {\mathfrak p}_0\), but \(f_1\) may not be the minimal polynomial of \(\beta\). By Nakayama's Lemma, \(R[\beta]=S\) if and only if \(R/{\mathfrak m}_R[\beta \bmod {\mathfrak m}_R] = S/{\mathfrak m}_R S\). Consider the following map of exact sequences:
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
             0 \arrow[r] & {\dfrac{ R[\beta]\cap {\mathfrak m}_S}{{\mathfrak m}_R[\beta]}} 
             \arrow[r]\arrow[d] & 
             {\dfrac{R}{{\mathfrak m}_R}[\beta \bmod {\mathfrak m}_R]} 
             \arrow[r]\arrow[d, hook] & \dfrac{R}{{\mathfrak m}_R}[\beta \bmod {\mathfrak m}_S] 
             \arrow[r]\arrow[d] 
            & 0\\
            0 \arrow[r] & \dfrac{{\mathfrak m}_S}{{\mathfrak m}_RS} \arrow[r] & \dfrac{S}{{\mathfrak m}_RS} \arrow[r] & \dfrac{S}{{\mathfrak m}_S} \arrow[r] & 0.
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]
        Since \(\beta\bmod {\mathfrak m}_R = \beta_0\bmod {\mathfrak m}_{R_0}\), the rightmost vertical map is a bijection. Additionally, since \(f_1(x)\bmod {\mathfrak m}_R\) 
        is the minimal polynomial of \(\beta_0\bmod{\mathfrak m}_R\), \(f_1(\beta) \in  R[\beta]\cap{\mathfrak q}_0\subset R[\beta]\cap {\mathfrak m}_S\). Thus, if \(f_1(\beta)\bmod{\mathfrak m}_R\) generates \({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R\)
        then the leftmost vertical arrow is a bijection and hence we have the desired equality.

        Assume that \(f_1(\beta)\bmod{\mathfrak m}_R\) does not generate \({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R S = ({\mathfrak q}_0 + {\mathfrak m}_RS)/{\mathfrak m}_R S\simeq  {\mathfrak q}_0/{\mathfrak m}_R S\cap {\mathfrak q}_0 = {\mathfrak q}_0/{\mathfrak p}_0S\). 
        By assumption, \(S\) is a regular local ring hence a unique factorization domain, so there exists a \(q_0\in S\) that generates the height \(1\) ideal \({\mathfrak q}_0\). 
        Since
        \(f_1(\beta)\) does not generate \({\mathfrak q}_0\), 
        \(f_1(\beta) = q_0a\) for some \(a\in {{\mathfrak m}_S}\) and so
        \[
        f_1(\beta + q_0)= f_1(\beta) + f_1'(\beta)q_0 + q_0^2b = q_0(a + f_1'(\beta) + q_0b),
        \]
        for some \(b\in S\). Further, since \(f_1'(\beta)\bmod {\mathfrak q}_0 = f_0'(\beta_0)\in S_0^{\times}\), \(f_1'(\beta)\notin {\mathfrak m}_S\); thus \(\langle f_1(\beta + q_0)\rangle = {\mathfrak q}_0\).
        Therefore, we may replace \(\beta\) with \(\beta + q_0\) and conclude that \(R[\beta] = S\).
nodes.statement_short: Lift a generator of the étale quotient S/q0 and, if needed, perturb β by a generator q0 so that f1(β) generates q0; then Nakayama gives R[β] = S.

nodes.name: Étale case: Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: If \(R\to S\) is \'etale, then we apply Lemma~\ref{lem:FiniteEtaleIsLocallyMonogenic}.

nodes.name: Non-étale case: set up quotient rings R0, S0
nodes.statement:
Henceforth we assume that \(R\to S\) is not \'etale and let \({\mathfrak p}_0 := {\mathfrak q}_0 \cap R \). 
        Denote $R_0:=R/{\mathfrak p}_0$, ${\mathfrak m}_{R_0}:={\mathfrak m}_R/{\mathfrak p}_0$, $S_0:=S/{\mathfrak p}_0$, and ${\mathfrak m}_{S_0}:={\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak p}_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Non-étale case: set up quotient rings R0, S0.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.2 on R0 → S0 gives β0; also m_S = q0 + m_R S
nodes.statement: By assumption, \(R_0  \to S_0\) is \'etale, so Lemma~\ref{lem:FiniteEtaleIsLocallyMonogenic} implies that there is \(\beta_0\in S_0\) such that \(R_0[\beta_0] = S_0\) and furthermore, that  \(f_0'(\beta_0) \in S_0^{\times}\) where \(f_0(x)\) denotes the minimal polynomial of \(\beta_0\). Moreover, since \(R_0\to S_0\) is \'etale, \({\mathfrak m}_{S_0} = {\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak q}_0 = {\mathfrak m}_{R_0} S_0 = ({\mathfrak m}_R/{\mathfrak p}_0)(S/{\mathfrak q}_0)\), i.e., \({\mathfrak m}_S = {\mathfrak q}_0 + {\mathfrak m}_RS \).
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.2 on R0 → S0 gives β0; also m_S = q0 + m_R S.

nodes.name: Lift β0 to β and f0 to monic f1
nodes.statement: Choose \(\beta\in S\) to be a lift of \(\beta_0\) and choose \(f_1(z)\in R[z]\) to be a monic lift of \(f_0\). Note that this implies that \(f_1\bmod {\mathfrak p}_0\) is the minimal polynomial of \(\beta\bmod {\mathfrak p}_0\), but \(f_1\) may not be the minimal polynomial of \(\beta\).
nodes.statement_short: Lift β0 to β and f0 to monic f1.

nodes.name: Reduce R[β] = S to the fiber over m_R
nodes.statement: By Nakayama's Lemma, \(R[\beta]=S\) if and only if \(R/{\mathfrak m}_R[\beta \bmod {\mathfrak m}_R] = S/{\mathfrak m}_R S\).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce R[β] = S to the fiber over m_R.

nodes.statement_short: Compare exact sequences for R[β] and S modulo m_R.

nodes.name: Right map bijective; if f1(β) generates m_S/m_R S the left map is too
nodes.statement:
Since \(\beta\bmod {\mathfrak m}_R = \beta_0\bmod {\mathfrak m}_{R_0}\), the rightmost vertical map is a bijection. Additionally, since \(f_1(x)\bmod {\mathfrak m}_R\) 
        is the minimal polynomial of \(\beta_0\bmod{\mathfrak m}_R\), \(f_1(\beta) \in  R[\beta]\cap{\mathfrak q}_0\subset R[\beta]\cap {\mathfrak m}_S\). Thus, if \(f_1(\beta)\bmod{\mathfrak m}_R\) generates \({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R\)
        then the leftmost vertical arrow is a bijection and hence we have the desired equality.

nodes.statement: By assumption, \(S\) is a regular local ring hence a unique factorization domain, so there exists a \(q_0\in S\) that generates the height \(1\) ideal \({\mathfrak q}_0\).
nodes.statement_short: S is a UFD, so q0 = (q0) is principal.

nodes.name: Taylor-expand f1(β + q0)
nodes.statement:
Since
        \(f_1(\beta)\) does not generate \({\mathfrak q}_0\), 
        \(f_1(\beta) = q_0a\) for some \(a\in {{\mathfrak m}_S}\) and so
        \[
        f_1(\beta + q_0)= f_1(\beta) + f_1'(\beta)q_0 + q_0^2b = q_0(a + f_1'(\beta) + q_0b),
        \]
        for some \(b\in S\).
nodes.statement_short: Taylor-expand f1(β + q0).

nodes.name: f1'(β) is a unit, so f1(β+q0) generates q0
nodes.statement: Further, since \(f_1'(\beta)\bmod {\mathfrak q}_0 = f_0'(\beta_0)\in S_0^{\times}\), \(f_1'(\beta)\notin {\mathfrak m}_S\); thus \(\langle f_1(\beta + q_0)\rangle = {\mathfrak q}_0\).
nodes.statement_short: f1'(β) is a unit, so f1(β+q0) generates q0.

nodes.name: Replace β by β+q0
nodes.statement: Therefore, we may replace \(\beta\) with \(\beta + q_0\) and conclude that \(R[\beta] = S\).
nodes.statement_short: Replace β by β+q0.

nodes.name: Presentation of the minimal polynomial of a monogenic generator
nodes.statement:
Retain the notation and assumptions from Lemma~\ref{lem:MonogenicLocal},  let \(f(z)\in R[z]\) be the minimal polynomial of \(\beta\), and let \({\mathfrak p}_0 := {\mathfrak q}_0\cap R\). Assume, in addition, that 
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item the map \(R\hookrightarrow S\) is not \'etale,
            \item there is an inclusion \({\mathcal O}_K\hookrightarrow R\) whose composition with the quotient \(R\to R/{\mathfrak p}_0\) yields an isomorphism \({\mathcal O}_K\xrightarrow{\sim}R/{\mathfrak p}_0\), and
            \item the prime \({\mathfrak q}_0\) is the unique prime lying over \({\mathfrak p}_0\).
        \end{enumerate} 
        Then, there exists a monic
        polynomial \(\tilde{f}\in {\mathcal O}_K[z]\) that is irreducible modulo \(\pi\) and an integer \(e>1\) such that 
        \[
            f - \tilde{f}^e = p_0 s\in R[z], 
        \]
        where \(p_0\in R\) is a generator of \({\mathfrak p}_0\) and \(s\in R[z]\) is such that \(s \bmod f\) is a unit in \(S\).
nodes.statement_short: Under the extra hypotheses, the minimal polynomial of β is f̃^e + p0 s with f̃ irreducible mod π, e > 1 and s a unit in S.

f - \tilde{f}^e = p_0 s\in R[z],

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:MonogenicLocal}, \(S\simeq R[z]/f(z) \) so \(S/{\mathfrak p}_0S \simeq (R/{\mathfrak p}_0)[z]/f(z)\bmod{\mathfrak p}_0\). Since \({\mathfrak q}_0\) is the unique prime lying over \({\mathfrak p}_0\), the image of the monic polynomial \(f\bmod {\mathfrak p}_0\) in \({\mathcal O}_K\) is a prime power.  Further, since \(R\hookrightarrow S\) is not \'etale at \({\mathfrak q}_0\), it is a nontrivial prime power, i.e., \(f\bmod {\mathfrak p}_0 = \tilde{f}(z)^e\) for some \(e>1\) and irreducible polynomial \(\tilde{f}\in {\mathcal O}_K[z]\).  Thus, \({\mathfrak q}_0 = {\mathfrak p}_0 S + \langle \tilde{f}\rangle\). Since \({\mathcal O}_K\simeq R/{\mathfrak p}_0 \to S/{\mathfrak q}_0 \simeq {\mathcal O}_K[z]/\tilde{f}(z)\) is \'etale and \({\mathcal O}_K\) is Henselian, the polynomial \(\tilde{f}\) must remain irreducible modulo \({\mathfrak m}_R\). In particular, \({\mathfrak m}_S = {\mathfrak m}_R S + \langle \tilde f\rangle \subset R[z]/f\).

        The assumption that \(S=R[z]/f\) is a regular local ring implies that \(f\notin ({\mathfrak m}_R[z] + \langle \tilde{f}\rangle)^2\) or equivalently (since \(e>1\)) that \(f - \tilde{f}^e\notin ({\mathfrak m}_R[z] + \langle \tilde{f}\rangle)^2\). Since \(f - \tilde{f}^e \in {\mathfrak p}_0[z]\subset {\mathfrak m}_R[z]\), for any generator \(p_0\) of \({\mathfrak p}_0\), we may write \( f - \tilde{f}^e = p_0 \cdot s \) for some \(s\in R[z]\) that is not in \({\mathfrak m}_R[z] + \langle\tilde{f}\rangle\). This implies that \(s \bmod f\in S\) is a unit, as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce f modulo p0 to a nontrivial prime power f̃^e via uniqueness of q0 and Henselianity; regularity of S forces the correction term p0 s with s a unit.

nodes.name: S = R[z]/f by Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:MonogenicLocal}, \(S\simeq R[z]/f(z) \) so \(S/{\mathfrak p}_0S \simeq (R/{\mathfrak p}_0)[z]/f(z)\bmod{\mathfrak p}_0\).
nodes.statement_short: S = R[z]/f by Lemma 3.1.

nodes.name: f mod p0 is a nontrivial prime power f̃^e
nodes.statement: Since \({\mathfrak q}_0\) is the unique prime lying over \({\mathfrak p}_0\), the image of the monic polynomial \(f\bmod {\mathfrak p}_0\) in \({\mathcal O}_K\) is a prime power.  Further, since \(R\hookrightarrow S\) is not \'etale at \({\mathfrak q}_0\), it is a nontrivial prime power, i.e., \(f\bmod {\mathfrak p}_0 = \tilde{f}(z)^e\) for some \(e>1\) and irreducible polynomial \(\tilde{f}\in {\mathcal O}_K[z]\).
nodes.statement_short: f mod p0 is a nontrivial prime power f̃^e.

nodes.statement: Thus, \({\mathfrak q}_0 = {\mathfrak p}_0 S + \langle \tilde{f}\rangle\).

nodes.name: Henselianity: f̃ irreducible mod m_R, so m_S = m_R S + (f̃)

In particular, \({\mathfrak m}_S = {\mathfrak m}_R S + \langle \tilde f\rangle \subset R[z]/f\).
nodes.statement_short: Henselianity: f̃ irreducible mod m_R, so m_S = m_R S + (f̃).

nodes.name: Regularity: f - f̃^e not in (m_R + (f̃))^2
nodes.statement: The assumption that \(S=R[z]/f\) is a regular local ring implies that \(f\notin ({\mathfrak m}_R[z] + \langle \tilde{f}\rangle)^2\) or equivalently (since \(e>1\)) that \(f - \tilde{f}^e\notin ({\mathfrak m}_R[z] + \langle \tilde{f}\rangle)^2\).

nodes.name: Write f - f̃^e = p0 s with s a unit in S
nodes.statement: Since \(f - \tilde{f}^e \in {\mathfrak p}_0[z]\subset {\mathfrak m}_R[z]\), for any generator \(p_0\) of \({\mathfrak p}_0\), we may write \( f - \tilde{f}^e = p_0 \cdot s \) for some \(s\in R[z]\) that is not in \({\mathfrak m}_R[z] + \langle\tilde{f}\rangle\). This implies that \(s \bmod f\in S\) is a unit, as desired.

nodes.name: Residue algebras of ramified monogenic extensions of 2-dimensional regular local rings
nodes.statement:
Let \(R\hookrightarrow S\) be a finite extension of \(2\)-dimensional regular local rings where \(R\supset {\mathcal O}_K\) and this extension is relative dimension \(1\). Assume that \(R\to S\) satisfies the assumptions of Lemmas~\ref{lem:MonogenicLocal} and~\ref{lem:RegularLocalRingPresentation}, which implies the existence of primes \({\mathfrak q}_0\subset S\) and \({\mathfrak p}_0:={\mathfrak q}_0\cap R \subset R\) such that \(R/{\mathfrak p}_0\to S/{\mathfrak q}_0\) is \'etale and \({\mathfrak q}_0\) is the unique prime lying over \({\mathfrak p}_0\).

    Then for any generator \(p_0\in R\) of \({\mathfrak p}_0\) there is a bijection:
    \begin{equation} {\mathcal O}_K\longleftrightarrow \left\{{\mathfrak p}\subset R :\textup{ht}({\mathfrak p}) = 1, {\mathcal O}_K\hookrightarrow R \to R/{\mathfrak p} \text{ is an isomorphism} \right\}, \; a\mapsto {\mathfrak p}_a:= \langle p_0 + \pi a\rangle.
    \end{equation}
    Further, for \(a\in {\mathcal O}_K \smallsetminus\{0\}\), the \'etale algebra 
    \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a}) := S_{{\mathfrak p}_a}/{\mathfrak p}_a S_{{\mathfrak p}_a}\) has the following properties. 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item \(\dim_{K} {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})  = e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R)\cdot [S/{\mathfrak m}_S : R/{\mathfrak m}_R]\). 
        
        \item Any maximal subfield \(L\subset {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})\) has inertia degree \(f(L/K)\geq [S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R]\).
        
        \item Any maximal subfield \(L\subset {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})\) has ramification degree $e(L/K)$ such that
        \[
        \frac{e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R)}{\gcd(1 + v(a), e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R))}\leq e(L/K)\leq e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R).
        \]
        
        \item If \(1 + v(a)\) is relatively prime to \(e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R)\) (or more generally if \(e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R) = e(L/K)\)), then \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})\) is a field with ramification degree equal to \(e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R)\) and inertia degree equal to \([S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R]\).
        
        \item Assume that \(e: = e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R)\) is coprime to \(q_K\), which by~\eqref{part:Ramification} implies that all maximal subfields \(L\subset {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})\) are tamely ramified over \(K\). Let \(K' := K([S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R])\) and fix a uniformizer \(\pi\) of \(K\). Then there exists a subgroup \({\mathcal O}_{K}^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}/{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}<H< {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times}/{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\) (necessarily cyclic) that completely characterizes the isomorphism classes of field extensions \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})/K\) for \({\mathfrak p}_a\) with \(1+v(a)\) coprime to \(e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R)\). More precisely:
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item If \(u\in {\mathcal O}_{K'}^\times\) generates \(H/{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\) and \(L/K'\) is a totally tamely ramified extension of degree \(e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R)\) with \(u\pi\in N_{L/K}(L^{\times})\), then there exists an \(a\in {\mathcal O}_K\) such that \(L\simeq {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_{a}})\).
            
            \item Conversely, if \(1+v(a)\) is coprime to \(e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R)\) and \(\varpi_{{\mathfrak p}_a}\in N_{{\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})/K'}({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})^{\times})\) is a uniformizer, then \(\varpi_{{\mathfrak p}_a}\pi^{-1}\) generates \(H/{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\).

            \item Furthermore, if \(a,a'\in{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\), then \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a}) \simeq {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_{a'}})\) if and only if \(a'a^{-1}\in {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\).
            In particular, there are \([{\mathcal O}_K^{\times} : {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\cap {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}]\) 
            isomorphism classes of totally tamely ramified degree $e$ extensions of $K'$ that can arise as ${\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})$ for some $a \in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}$; and for every $L/K'$ that arises, 
            \[
                \mu_{{\mathcal O}_K}(\{ a \in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times} : 
                {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})\simeq L\}) = \mu_{{\mathcal O}_K}({\mathcal O}_K^{\times})\mu_{{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}}({\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\cap {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e})=
                \frac{q_K-1}{q_K}\cdot\frac1{[{\mathcal O}_K^{\times} : {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\cap {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}]}.
            \]
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Height 1 primes p_a = (p0 + πa) with O_K-quotient are parametrized by a; the residue algebra k(S_{p_a}) has computable dimension, inertia, ramification bounds and tame isomorphism classes.

nodes.name: Lifting coprime factorizations modulo π^v
nodes.statement:
Let \(K\) be a nonarchimedean local field and let \(g_1,g_2, \tilde{g_1}, \tilde{g_2}\in {\mathcal O}_{K}[z]\) be monic polynomials such that \(\deg(g_i) = \deg(\tilde{g}_i)\), \(g_i\equiv \tilde{g}_i\bmod \pi\) for \(i=1,2\)  and \(\gcd(g_1\bmod \pi,g_2\bmod \pi)= 1\).
    If \(g_1g_2 \equiv \tilde{g_1}\tilde{g_2}\bmod \pi^v\) for some positive integer \(v\), then 
    \(
    g_i\equiv \tilde{g_i}\bmod \pi^v
    \) for \(i = 1,2.\)

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement:
We prove this by induction; the base case is given by assumption. Fix \(1\leq n < v\) and assume that \(\tilde{g_i}\equiv g_i\bmod \pi^n\), i.e., that \(\tilde{g_i} = g_i + \pi^n m_i \) for some polynomials \(m_i\) with \(\deg(m_i) < \deg(g_i)\). Then
    \(
    \tilde{g_1}\tilde{g_2} = g_1g_2 + \pi^n(m_1g_2 + m_2g_1) + \pi^{2n}m_1m_2 \equiv g_1g_2\pmod{\pi^v}.
    \)
    Since \(v>n\geq1\), this implies that \(m_1g_2 + m_2g_1\equiv 0\bmod \pi\). By assumption \(g_1\bmod \pi\) and \(g_2\bmod \pi\) are relatively prime, so \(g_i|m_i\) modulo \(\pi\). Since \(\deg(m_i)<\deg(g_i)\), we must have \(m_i\equiv 0 \bmod \pi\).
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the exponent n: the first-order term m1 g2 + m2 g1 vanishes mod π, and coprimality with degree bounds forces m_i ≡ 0.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.4
nodes.statement:
Let \({\mathfrak p}\subset R\) be a height \(1\) prime (hence principal) such that \({\mathcal O}_K\simeq R/{\mathfrak p}\). Thus, there exists an \(a'\in {\mathcal O}_K\) such that \(-a'\equiv p_0 \bmod {\mathfrak p}\), i.e., \(p_0 + a'= pr\) for some \(r\in R\) and generator \(p\) of \({\mathfrak p}\). 
    Since \(R/{\mathfrak p}_0\) is also isomorphic to \({\mathcal O}_K\), there exists an \(a_0\in {\mathcal O}_K\) such that \(p - a_0 = p_0r_0\) for some \(r_0\in R\). Hence, 
    \[
        prr_0 = p_0r_0 + a'r_0 = p - a_0 + a'r_0, \quad \textup{and} \quad
    p_0rr_0 = pr - a_0r = p_0 + a' - a_0r
    \]
    so \(a_0 = a'\cdot(r_0\bmod {\mathfrak p})\in {\mathcal O}_K\) and \(a' = a_0\cdot(r\bmod {\mathfrak p}_0)\in {\mathcal O}_K\).  In particular, \(r_0\bmod {\mathfrak p} \) and \(r\bmod {\mathfrak p}_0\) are units in \({\mathcal O}_K\). Since \(R\) is local, this implies that \(r, r_0\in R^{\times}\) and so \({\mathfrak p} = \langle pr\rangle = \langle p_0 + a'\rangle\). Moreover, since \({\mathfrak p} + {\mathfrak p}_0\subset {\mathfrak m}_R\), we have \(a'\in \pi{\mathcal O}_K\), i.e., \({\mathfrak p} = {\mathfrak p}_a:= \langle p_0 + a\pi\rangle\) for some \(a\in {\mathcal O}_K\) as desired. 

    By Lemma~\ref{lem:MonogenicLocal}, \(S = R[\beta] \simeq R[z]/f(z)\), where \(f(z)\) is the minimal polynomial of \(\beta\). 
    Since \(R\to S\) is not \'etale and the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:RegularLocalRingPresentation} are satisfied, there is a monic polynomial \(\tilde{f}\in {\mathcal O}_K[z]\), irreducible modulo \(\pi\), such that \(f - \tilde{f}^e = p_0 s\) for some \(e>1\), \(s\in R[z]\) whose image in \(S\) is a unit. From this presentation, we can conclude 
    part~\eqref{part:Dimension}. Since \(f \bmod {\mathfrak m}_R = (f\bmod {\mathfrak p}_a)\bmod \pi \equiv \tilde{f}^e\), the field \(L\) contains the unramified extension of degree equal to \(\deg(\tilde{f})\).  Moreover, since \({\mathfrak m}_S = {\mathfrak m}_R S + \langle\tilde{f}\rangle\), we conclude \([S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R] = \deg(\tilde{f})\), proving~\eqref{part:Inertia}.

    Now we consider part~\eqref{part:Ramification}; by part~\eqref{part:Inertia}, \(L\) contains \(K':=K([S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R])\) so it suffices to compute \(e(L/K')\). Let \(\theta_i\in K'\) denote the roots of \(\tilde{f}\). Recall the relation of \(f\) given in Lemma~\ref{lem:RegularLocalRingPresentation}, i.e., \(f= \tilde{f}^e + p_0s\) where \(e = e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R)\). Note that \(s\) depends only on \(f\) and \({\mathfrak p}_0\); it does not depend on \({\mathfrak p}_a\). Then we have
    \begin{equation} f - \tilde{f}^e = p_0s = (p - a\pi)s. 
    \end{equation}
    Since \(f\bmod {\mathfrak p}_a\) has the same reduction modulo \(\pi\) as \(\tilde{f}^e = \prod_i(z - \theta_i)^e\), Hensel's lemma implies that \(f(z)\bmod {\mathfrak p}_a\) factors as \(h_1h_2\dots h_r\), where each \(h_i\in {\mathcal O}_{K'}[z]\) is monic and \(h_i\equiv (z - \theta_i)^e\bmod \pi\). In particular, \(L\) is obtained from \(K'\) by adjoining the root of a degree \(e\) polynomial, so \(e(L/K')\leq e = e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R) \).

    Setting \(v := 1 + v(a)\) and \(u:= a\pi^{1-v} \in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\), the above equalities and congruences yield:
    \[
        h_1(z)\cdots h_r(z) \equiv f\bmod {\mathfrak p}_a = \tilde{f}^e - u\pi^{v} s = (z- \theta_1)^e\cdots (z - \theta_r)^e - u\pi^v s.
    \]
    Since for \(i\neq j\), \(h_i\equiv (z - \theta_i)^e\pmod \pi\) is relatively prime to \(h_j\equiv (z - \theta_j)^e\pmod \pi\) and \(h_i,h_j, (z-\theta_i)^e, (z-\theta_j)^e\) are all monic of degree \(e\), Lemma~\ref{lem:LiftingFactorizations} implies that \(h_i(z) \equiv (z - \theta_i)^e\pmod{\pi^v}\) for all \(i\). In particular, if we set \(\theta := \theta_1\) and \(g(z):= h_1(z + \theta_1)\), then \(g(z) \equiv z^e\bmod \pi^v\) in \(R/{\mathfrak p}_a[\theta, z] \simeq{\mathcal O}_{K'}[z]\).  Furthermore, by \eqref{eq:fmodulop}
    \begin{equation}
        g(0) = (f\bmod{\mathfrak p}_a)(\theta)\prod_{i=2}^rh_i(\theta)^{-1} = -u\pi^vs(\theta)\prod_{i=2}^rh_i(\theta)^{-1} 
        \equiv -u\pi^vs(\theta)\prod_{i=2}^r(\theta - \theta_i)^{-e}\bmod \pi^{v+1} \end{equation}
    Since \(s\in R[z]\) gives a unit in \(S\), \(s(\theta)\in {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times}\). Thus, the Newton polygon of \(g\) has a single segment of slope \(-\frac{v}{e}\), which gives the desired lower bound in~\eqref{part:Ramification}.
     
    Furthermore, if \(e(L/K) = e\) (which is implied if \(v\) is relatively prime to \(e\)), then combining~\eqref{part:Dimension} and~\eqref{part:Inertia} we have
    \[
        e\cdot [S/{\mathfrak m}_S: R/{\mathfrak m}_R] = \dim_K {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a}) \geq \dim_K L = e(L/K)f(L/K) \geq e \cdot [S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R].
    \]
    Thus, \(L = {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})\) and \(f(L/K) = [S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R]\), which proves~\eqref{part:DistancefrakptoB}.
    
    
    Finally, we prove part~\eqref{part:RamIsom}. Retain all the notation from above and assume that \(q_K\) is coprime to $e$; in particular, by~\eqref{part:Ramification}, \(L/K\) is tamely ramified. Since the maximal unramified subextension of \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})/K\) is \(K'/K\), it suffices to show that there is a subgroup \(H\) that characterizes the isomorphism classes of totally tamely ramified field extensions \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})/K'\). We claim this subgroup is \(H := \langle s(\theta) \rangle{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}/{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\).
    
    By Proposition~\ref{prop:IsoTotTamelyRam}, the isomorphism class of \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})/K'\) is determined by a uniformizer in \(N_{{\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})/K'}({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})^{\times})\) modulo \({\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\). From the bijection in \eqref{eq:OK-primes}, we must understand how a uniformizer in the norm subgroup of \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})/K'\) depends on \(a = u\pi^{v-1}\) (recall that \({\mathfrak p}_a = \langle p_0 + a\pi\rangle\)). 
    We computed above that \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})/K'\) is generated by adjoining a root of \(g(z)\) and thus \((-1)^eg(0)\in N_{{\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})/K'}({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})^{\times})\). Since \(K'^{\times e}\) is contained in the norm subgroup,~\eqref{eq:g0} shows that the norm subgroup contains the uniformizer
    \(
        \left(-us(\theta)\right)^{m_v} \pi,
    \)
    where \(m_v\) is a multiplicative inverse of \(v\) modulo \(e\).  
    
    Let us consider~\eqref{part:CurvePartitionByv}. If \(a,a'\in {\mathcal O}_{K}^{\times}\) (so \(u = a\) and \(u' = a'\)), then \(-us(\theta)\equiv -u's(\theta)\bmod {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\) if and only if \(u'u^{-1}\in {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\). Thus, \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a}) \simeq {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_{a'}})\) if and only if \(a'a^{-1}\in {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\). In particular, the totally tamely ramified degree \(e\) extensions of \(K'\) that can appear as \({\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})\) for some \(a\in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\) are in bijection with \({\mathcal O}_K^{\times}/{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\cap {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\). 
    Moreover, for a fixed \(a_0\in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\),
    \begin{align*}
        \mu_{{\mathcal O}_K}\left(\left\{a\in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times} : \;{\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_a})\simeq {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}_{a_0}}) \right\}\right) & =  \mu_{{\mathcal O}_K}\left(\left\{a\in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times} : aa_0^{-1}\in {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e} \right\}\right) \\& = \mu_{{\mathcal O}_K}({\mathcal O}_K^{\times})\mu_{{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}}\left(a_0 ({\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\cap{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}) \right)\\
        & = \mu_{{\mathcal O}_K}({\mathcal O}_K^{\times})\mu_{{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}}\left({\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\cap{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e} \right)\\
        & = \frac{q_K-1}{q_K}\cdot\frac1{[{\mathcal O}_K^{\times} : {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\cap {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}]}.
    \end{align*}
    
    To prove the rest of~\eqref{part:RamIsom} it remains to prove the following statements:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[\eqref{part:Existence}] If \(\tilde{u}\in H\) generates \(H/{\mathcal O}_{K}^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\), then there exists a \(u\in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\) and \(v\in \mathbb{N}\) such that \(\left(-u s(\theta)\right)^{m_{v}}\tilde{u}^{-1}\in {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\).
        
        \item[\eqref{part:Uniqueness}] If \(u\in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\) and \(v\in \mathbb{N}\), then \(\langle\left(-us(\theta)\right)^{m_v}\rangle\) generates \(H/{\mathcal O}_{K}^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\).
    \end{enumerate}
    Let \(\tilde{u}\in H\) be an element that generates \(H/{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\), i.e., \(\tilde{u}^v = -u s(\theta)u'^e\) for some integer \(v\) that is coprime to \(e\), some \(u\in {\mathcal O}_{K}^{\times}\), and some \(u'\in {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times}\). Taking the \(m_v^{th}\) power of both sides yields~\eqref{part:Existence}.

    Let \(u\in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\) and \(v\in \mathbb{N}\). Since \(m_v\) is an inverse of \(v\) modulo \(e\), \(\langle\left(-us(\theta)\right)^{m_v}\rangle = \langle-us(\theta)\rangle \subset {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}/{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\), and this in turn equals \(H\) modulo \({\mathcal O}_{K}^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\). Thus we have~\eqref{part:Uniqueness}.
nodes.statement_short: Use the presentation f = f̃^e + p0 s; reduce modulo p_a, factor by Hensel and Lemma 3.6, and read ramification from the Newton polygon of g(z) = h1(z+θ). Tame isomorphism classes follow from Proposition 2.1 via the norm of a root of g.

nodes.name: Ramification and inertia degrees of fibers of good-reduction morphisms
nodes.statement:
Let \(\psi\colon C \to D\) be a morphism between smooth projective geometrically integral curves that has good reduction,  let \(t\in (D-B)(K)\), let $\overline{t}$ be the specialization of $t$, and let \(\overline{x}\in {\mathcal C}_{\overline{t}}\). Define
    \[
        v(t, {\mathcal B}) := \begin{cases}
            \max_{t_0\in B(K)}\left\{n : t= t_0 \in {\mathcal D} ({\mathcal O}_K/\pi^n)\right\} & \textup{if }e(\overline{x}/\overline{t}) > 1, \\
            \infty & \textup{otherwise}.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    \noindent Then: 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item \(\dim_K {\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}} = e({\overline{x}/\overline{t}})\deg(\overline{x})\). \item Any maximal subfield \(L\subset{\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}}\) has inertia degree \(f(L/K)\geq\deg(\overline{x})\).
        \item Any maximal subfield \(L\subset{\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}}\) has ramification degree 
        \[
        \frac{e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})}{\gcd(v(t, {\mathcal B}), e(\overline{x}/\overline{t}))}\leq e(L/K)\leq e(\overline{x}/\overline{t}).
        \]
        \item If \(v(t,{\mathcal B})\) is relatively prime to \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\) (or, more generally, if \(e(L/K) = e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\)), then \({\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}}\) is a field with ramification degree equal to \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\) and inertia degree equal to \(\deg(\overline{x})\). \item Assume that \(e: = e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\) is coprime to \(q_K\), which by~\eqref{part:Ramification} implies that all maximal subfields \(L\subset {\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}}\) are tamely ramified over \(K\). Let \(K' := K(\deg \overline{x})\) and fix a uniformizer \(\pi\) of \(K\).
        Then there exists a subgroup \({\mathcal O}_{K}^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}/{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}<H< {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times}/{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\) (necessarily cyclic) that completely characterizes the isomorphism classes of field extensions
        \({\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}}\) for \(t\) with \(v(t,{\mathcal B})\) coprime to \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\).
        More precisely:
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item If \(u\in {\mathcal O}_{K'}^\times\) generates \(H/{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\) and \(L/K'\) is a totally tamely ramified extension of degree \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\) with \(u\pi\in N_{L/K}(L^{\times})\), then there exists a \(t \in (D\smallsetminus B)(K)\) with \(t\rightsquigarrow\overline{t}\) such that \(L\simeq {\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}}\).
            
            \item Conversely, if \(v(t,{\mathcal B})\) is relatively prime to \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\) and \(\varpi_{{\mathfrak p}}\in N_{{\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}}/K'}({\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}}^{\times})\) is a uniformizer, then \(\varpi_{{\mathfrak p}}\pi^{-1}\) generates \(H/{\mathcal O}_K^{\times}{\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}\).


            \item Furthermore, there are \([{\mathcal O}_K^{\times} : {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\cap {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}]\) 
            isomorphism classes of totally tamely ramified degree $e$ extensions of $K'$ that can arise as ${\mathbf k}(C_{t_0})_{\overline{x}}$ for some $t_0 \in {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}$; and for every such ${\mathbf k}(C_{t_0})_{\overline{x}}$, 
            then
            \[
            \mu_{D}\left(\left\{t\in (D\smallsetminus B)(K) : t\rightsquigarrow\overline{t_0}, \; v(t,{\mathcal B}) = 1, \;{\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}}\simeq {\mathbf k}(C_{t_0})_{\overline{x}}\right\}\right) = \frac{q_K-1}{q_K}
            \cdot\frac1{[{\mathcal O}_K^{\times} : {\mathcal O}_K^{\times}\cap {\mathcal O}_{K'}^{\times e}]}.
            \]
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}

Let \(\psi_0 \colon C_0 \to D_0\) be a degree \(d\) morphism of smooth projective geometrically integral curves over a finite field \({\mathbb F}\), let \(\widehat\psi_0\colon \widehat{C}_0\to D_0\) be the Galois closure of \(\psi_0\), let \(G\) be its Galois group and let $\overline{t} \in D$ such that \(\psi_0\) is \'etale at \(\overline{t}\).
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item The Galois closure \(\widehat\psi_0\) is also \'etale at \(\overline{t}\) so
            there is a Frobenius conjugacy class \(c_{\overline{t}}\subset S_{d}\).
            \item If $(d_i)_{i=1}^r\vdash d$ is the cycle type of an element in \(c_{\overline{t}}\), then \[
                {\mathbf k}(({C}_0)_{\overline{t}}) \simeq \prod_{i=1}^r {\mathbf k}(\overline{t})(d_i).
            \]
            \item Let \(U_0\subset D_0\) be the smooth locus of \(\psi_0\) and let \((d_i)\vdash d\) be a partition. Then
            \[
                \frac{\#\left\{\overline{t} \in U_0({\mathbb F}) : {\mathbf k}(({C}_0)_{\overline{t}})\simeq \prod {\mathbb F}(d_i)\right\}}{\#U_0({\mathbb F})} = \frac{\#\left\{\sigma\in G : \mathrm{ct}(\sigma) = (d_i)\right\}}{|G|} + O\left(|{\mathbb F}|^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right),
            \]
            where the implied constant in the $O$ depends on the genus of $\widehat{C}_0$, the genus of $D_0$, and the group \(G\).
            \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement:
For $g\in G$, let \(\ell(g)\) denote the order of the orbit of \(d\) under \(g\), i.e., in the cycle representation of \(g\), $d$ is in a cycle of length $\ell(g)$. Then \(g^n\in G_0\) if and only if $n$ is a multiple of $\ell(g)$, so $|\langle g \rangle G_0/G_0|=\ell(g)$. We label the cycles of $\sigma$ such that the $i$-th cycle has length $d_i$. By transitivity for each $1\leq i\leq r$, there is a $g_i\in G$ that conjugates the $i$-th cycle of $\sigma$ to a cycle containing $d$. Thus, by the argument above, \(|\langle g_i \sigma  g_i^{-1}\rangle G_0/G_0| = d_i\). 

        Now let \(g\in G\) and let \(i\) be such that \(g\) conjugates the cycle containing $d$ to the $i$-th cycle of \(\sigma\). In other words, there exists some integer \(j\) such that \(g\sigma^jg_i^{-1} \in G_0\). Thus \(g_1, \dots, g_r\) give a complete set of double coset representatives.
nodes.statement_short: Orbit length of d under g gives |<g>G0/G0|; conjugating each cycle to contain d gives representatives, which exhaust the double cosets.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.6
nodes.statement:
The rings \(R := {\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal D}, \overline{t}}\) and \(S := {\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal C}, \overline{x}}\) are regular local rings because (by Definition~\ref{def:GoodReductionOfCurves}\eqref{gr:smoothmodel}) \({\mathcal C}\) and \({\mathcal D}\) are smooth \({\mathcal O}_K\)-schemes.  
        Definition~\ref{def:GoodReductionOfCurves}\eqref{gr:flatmorphism} implies that \(\Psi\) induces a finite extension of rings \(R\hookrightarrow S\).  

        If \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t}) = 1\), then \({\mathfrak m}_R S = {\mathfrak m}_S\). Since any extension of finite fields is separable, \(R\to S\) is \'etale at \({\mathfrak m}_S\). Since \(S\) is local, this implies that \(R\to S\) is \'etale at all primes.

        Now assume that \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})>1\). This implies that \(\overline{x}\in{\mathcal Z}\) so by purity of the ramification locus, \({\mathcal Z}\cap \mathrm{Spec} S\) is cut out by a nonzero ideal \(I\) that is contained in some height \(1\) prime ideal.  
        By Definition~\ref{def:GoodReductionOfCurves}\eqref{gr:etaleramification}, \({\mathcal O}_K \to R/I\cap R\) and \(R/I\cap R \to S/I\) are both \'etale. Thus \(S/I\) is an \'etale local extension of \({\mathcal O}_K\) and hence is isomorphic to \({\mathcal O}_{K(d)}\) for some \(d\). In particular, \(I\) is a prime ideal \({\mathfrak q}_0\), or, equivalently, there is a 
        unique codimension \(1\) point \(x\in {\mathcal C}\) that specializes to \(\overline{x}\) for which \(\psi\) is ramified.
        
        Set \({\mathfrak p}_0 := {\mathfrak q}_0 \cap R\). By the above paragraph, we have \({\mathcal O}_K\to R/{\mathfrak p}_0\) and \(R/{\mathfrak p}_0 \to S/{\mathfrak q}_0\) are \'etale. In particular, \(R/{\mathfrak p}_0\) is the maximal order of an unramified field extension of \(K\) and thus, \([R/{\mathfrak p}_0:{\mathcal O}_K] = \deg(\overline{t})\). Thus, we have~\eqref{property:etale}. 
        
        It remains to prove that \({\mathfrak p}_0 S\) is contained in a unique height \(1\) prime ideal (necessarily \({\mathfrak q}_0\)). By Definition~\ref{def:GoodReductionOfCurves}\eqref{gr:flatmorphism}, \(S\) is a flat \(R\)-module (see, e.g.,~\cite{QingLiu}*{Chapter 4, Remark 3.11}), hence free. Thus,
        \begin{align*}
            [S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R]e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R) & = \dim_{R/{\mathfrak m}_R}S/{\mathfrak m}_R S = \mathrm{rank}_R S = \dim_{{\mathbf k}(R_{{\mathfrak p}_0})}S_{{\mathfrak p}_0}/{\mathfrak p}_0 S_{{\mathfrak p}_0}\\
            & = \sum_{{\mathfrak q} |{\mathfrak p}_0} \dim_{{\mathbf k}(R_{{\mathfrak p}_0})}S_{{\mathfrak q}}/{\mathfrak p}_0 S_{{\mathfrak q}}
            = \sum_{{\mathfrak q}|{\mathfrak p}_0}[S_{{\mathfrak q}}/{\mathfrak q}:R_{{\mathfrak p}_0}/{\mathfrak p}_0]e({\mathfrak q} S_{{\mathfrak q}}/{\mathfrak p}_0R_{{\mathfrak p}_0}).
        \end{align*}
        By definition of \({\mathfrak q}_0\), if \({\mathfrak q}|{\mathfrak p}_0\) and \({\mathfrak q}\neq {\mathfrak q}_0\) then \(R\to S\) is \'etale at \({\mathfrak q}\), hence \(e({\mathfrak q} S_{{\mathfrak q}}/{\mathfrak p}_0R_{{\mathfrak p}_0}) = 1\) and \([S_{{\mathfrak q}}/{\mathfrak q}:R_{{\mathfrak p}_0}/{\mathfrak p}_0] = [S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R]\). Moreover, \({\mathcal O}_K \to S/{\mathfrak q}_0\) is \'etale, so \([S_{{\mathfrak q}_0}/{\mathfrak q}_0:R_{{\mathfrak p}_0}/{\mathfrak p}_0] = [S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R]\). Thus the above equation simplifies to
        \[
            e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R) 
            = e({\mathfrak q}_0 S_{{\mathfrak q}_0}/{\mathfrak p}_0R_{{\mathfrak p}_0}) + \#\{{\mathfrak q}|{\mathfrak p}_0 : {\mathfrak q}\neq {\mathfrak q}_0 \}\geq e({\mathfrak q}_0 S_{{\mathfrak q}_0}/{\mathfrak p}_0R_{{\mathfrak p}_0}).
        \]
        Geometrically, we may phrase this as \(e(x/t)\leq e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\) and \(\deg(x) = \deg(\overline{x})\) where \(x\in {\mathcal C}\) is the unique codimension \(1\) point that specializes to \(\overline{x}\) and is ramified. It remains to prove that \(e(x/t) = e(\overline{x}/\overline{t}).\)

        Now we work globally, i.e., considering the entire curve. The above relations give the inequality:
        \[
            \sum_{\overline{x}\in C_0} \sum_{\substack{x\in C\\ x\rightsquigarrow \overline{x}}} (e(x/t) - 1)\deg(x) \leq \sum_{\overline{x}\in C_0} 
            (e(\overline{x}/\overline{t}) - 1)\deg(\overline{x}).
        \]
        The left-hand side is the degree of the ramification divisor of \(\psi\) and the right-hand side is the degree of the ramification divisor of \(\psi_0\). By the Riemann-Hurwitz equation, these degrees are equal to \(2g(C) - 2 + 2\deg(\psi)\) and \(2g(C_0) - 2 + 2\deg(\psi_0)\), respectively.
        Since \({\mathcal C} \to \mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_K\) is smooth, \(g(C) = g(C_0)\) and since \(\Psi\) is finite \(\deg(\psi) = \deg(\psi_0)\). Thus we obtain the desired equality of ramification indices.
nodes.statement_short: Regularity from smoothness; purity of the branch locus and étaleness of Z give a unique ramified prime; a rank count plus Riemann-Hurwitz forces equality of ramification indices.

nodes.name: Local monogenic structure of good-reduction covers
nodes.statement:
Let \(\psi\colon C \to D\) be a morphism of good reduction,  let \(\Psi\colon{\mathcal C}\to {\mathcal D}\) be the associated integral model, let $\overline{t}\in {\mathcal D}$ be a closed point, and let $\overline{x}\in {\mathcal C}_{\overline{t}}$. In particular, for all $t\in D \smallsetminus B$ that specialize to $\overline{t}$, we have
        \[
                {\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}} \simeq \frac{{\mathbf k}(t)[z]}{\langle f_{\overline{x}}(z) \bmod {\mathfrak p}_t\rangle}, 
        \]
        where ${\mathfrak p}_t$ is the prime ideal corresponding to $t$ of the local ring ${\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal D}, \overline{t}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.2
nodes.statement:
Let \(R := {\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal D},\overline{t}}\).  By Corollary~\ref{cor:LocalStructure}, there exists a monic irreducible polynomial $f_{\overline{x}}\in R[z]$ such that  \({\mathcal O}_{{\mathcal C}, \overline{x}}\simeq R[z]/f_{\overline{x}}\), and 
        \[
                {\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}} \simeq \frac{{\mathbf k}(t)[z]}{\langle f_{\overline{x}}(z) \bmod {\mathfrak p}_t\rangle}. 
        \]
        If \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t}) = 1\), then \(f_{\overline{x}}\bmod {\mathfrak m}_R\) is a separable irreducible polynomial of degree equal to \(\deg f_{\overline{x}}\). Thus, for any prime \({\mathfrak p}\subset R\), \(f_{\overline{x}}\bmod {\mathfrak p}\) is irreducible and so \({\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}}\) is an unramified field extension of \(K\) of degree equal to \(\deg(f_{\overline{x}}) = \deg(f_{\overline{x}}\bmod {\mathfrak m}_R) = \deg(\overline{x})\), as desired. (Alternatively, see Section~\ref{sec:UnramifiedCase}.)

        Now assume that \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})>1\). Then \(R\to S\) is not \'etale. By Lemma~\ref{lem:GoodReductionConseq}, there exists a height one prime \({\mathfrak p}_0\subset R\) such that: there is a unique prime \({\mathfrak q}_0\) lying over \({\mathfrak p}_0\), \(R\to S\) is \'etale at all primes not containing \({\mathfrak q}_0\), and the maps \({\mathcal O}_K\to R/{\mathfrak p}_0\) and \(R/{\mathfrak p}_0\to S/{\mathfrak q}_0\) are \'etale.
        Since \(R/{\mathfrak m}_R = {\mathbf k}(\overline{t}) = {\mathbb F}\), this implies that \({\mathcal O}_K \to R/{\mathfrak p}_0\) is an isomorphism. Moreover, this implies that there is a unique \(t_0\in B(K)\) such that \(t_0 \bmod \pi\equiv \overline{t}\). Thus,
        we may apply Proposition~\ref{prop:RamifiedLocalPresentation} with \({\mathfrak p} = {\mathfrak p}_a\) the height one prime of \(R\) corresponding to \(t\). Furthermore, we have the following equalities: 
        \[
            {\mathbf k}(S_{{\mathfrak p}})  = {\mathbf k}(C_t)_{\overline{x}},\;
            \deg(\overline{x}) = [S/{\mathfrak m}_S:R/{\mathfrak m}_R],\;
            e(\overline{x}/\overline{t}) = e({\mathfrak m}_S/{\mathfrak m}_R), \;\textup{and}\;
            v(t, {\mathcal B})  = 1 + v(a).
        \]
        Therefore, Proposition~\ref{prop:RamifiedLocalPresentation} directly translates to Theorem~\ref{thm:RamAndInertiaDegrees}.
\qed

nodes.name: Good reduction away from finitely many places
nodes.statement:
Let \(C\) be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a number field \(k\) and let \(\psi\colon C \to {\mathbb P}^1_k\) be a nonconstant morphism.
    Then there exists a finite set of places \(T\subset \Omega_k\) containing all archimedean places where \(\psi\) has good reduction for all \(v\in \Omega_k\smallsetminus T.\)

    If the Galois closure \(\widehat\psi\colon \widehat C \to {\mathbb P}^1_k\) of \(\psi\) is geometrically integral, then we may enlarge \(T\) to assume that \(\hat \psi\) also has good reduction for all \(v\in \Omega_k\smallsetminus T.\) Then, for all \(v\in \Omega_k\smallsetminus T\), the special fiber of \(\widehat {\mathcal C}\) is the Galois closure of the special fiber of \({\mathcal C}\to {\mathbb P}^1_{{\mathcal O}_v}\) with Galois group \(\mathrm{Gal}(\widehat{C}/{\mathbb P}^1)\).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement:
This is a spreading out argument (see, e.g.,~\cite{PoonenRaPt}*{Section 3.2}). We provide the details in this situation for the reader's convenience.

We first spread out $C$ and \(\widehat C\) to schemes ${\mathcal C}$ and $\widehat{\mathcal C}$ over a dense open subscheme $\mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_{k, T}$ of $\mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_k$ as in \cite{PoonenRaPt}*{Theorem 3.2.1(i)}, so that the generic fiber  ${\mathcal C}_k$ is isomorphic to $C$. By~\cite{PoonenRaPt}*{Theorem 3.2.1(ii) and Table 1, page 306-307}, which references~\citelist{\cite{EGA4-4}*{17.7.8(ii)} \cite{EGA4-3}*{9.7.7(iv) and 8.10.5(xii)}}\, we may further enlarge \(T\) and impose that \({\mathcal C}\to \mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_{k, T}\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal C}\to \mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_{k, T}\) are smooth and proper
and that the fibers are geometrically integral.

Now we apply~\cite{PoonenRaPt}*{Theorem 3.2.1(iii)} to spread out $\psi$ and \(\widehat\psi\), so, after possibly enlarging \(T\), we obtain morphisms $\widehat\Psi\colon \widehat{\mathcal C}\rightarrow {\mathbb P}^1_{{\mathcal O}_{k, T}}$ and $\Psi\colon {\mathcal C}\rightarrow {\mathbb P}^1_{{\mathcal O}_{k, T}}$ such that \(\widehat\Psi\) factors through \(\Psi\). Further~\cite{PoonenRaPt}*{Theorem 3.2.1(iv) and Table 1, page 306-307}, which references~\cite{EGA4-3}*{11.2.6(ii)}, implies that we may assume that \(\widehat \Psi\) and \(\Psi\) are flat (again, at the expense of possibly enlarging \(T\)). There are only finitely many places of \(k\) lying over the primes bounded by \(\deg(\widehat\psi)\), so after adding these finitely many places to \(T\), we have verified Definition~\ref{def:GoodReductionOfCurves}\eqref{gr:smoothmodel} and~\eqref{gr:flatmorphism}.

Now we turn to verifying Definition~\ref{def:GoodReductionOfCurves}\eqref{gr:etaleramification}. Since there is no nontrivial \'etale cover of ${\mathbb P}^1_k$ and \(C\) is geometrically integral, the morphism \(\psi\) cannot be \'etale, but it is generically \'etale since \(\mathrm{char}(k) = 0\). Thus, there is a minimal proper smooth closed subscheme \(Z\subset C\) and \(\widehat Z\subset \widehat C\) such that \(\psi\) and \(\widehat\psi\) are \'etale away from \(Z\) and \(\widehat Z\), respectively. Let \({\mathcal Z}\subset {\mathcal C}\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal Z}\subset \widehat{\mathcal C}\) be the Zariski closure of \(Z\) and \(\widehat Z\) respectively. Since each map in \({\mathcal Z} \to \Psi({\mathcal Z})\to\mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_{k,T}\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal Z} \to \Psi(\widehat{\mathcal Z})\to\mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_{k,T}\) is generically \'etale, as above we may use~\cite{PoonenRaPt}*{Theorem 3.2.1(ii) and Table 1, page 306-307}, which references~\cite{EGA4-4}*{17.7.8(ii)}, to assume (after possibly enlarging \(T\)) that each of the four morphisms \({\mathcal Z} \to \Psi({\mathcal Z})\to\mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_{k,T}\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal Z} \to  \Psi(\widehat{\mathcal Z})\to\mathrm{Spec} {\mathcal O}_{k,T}\) are \'etale.

It remains to prove the claim about the Galois group. Let \(v\in \Omega_k\smallsetminus T\). We have a finite morphism \(\widehat\Psi \colon \widehat{\mathcal C} \to {\mathbb P}^1_{{\mathcal O}_v}\) whose extension of function fields is Galois. Since the special fiber is geometrically irreducible, the decomposition group of the special fiber is equal to \(\mathrm{Gal}(\widehat{C}/{\mathbb P}^1_{k_v})\) and similarly, the decomposition group of the special fiber of \(\widehat  {\mathcal C} \to {\mathcal C}\) is equal to \(\mathrm{Gal}(\widehat{C}/C)\). Thus, the special fiber of \(\widehat{\Psi}\) is Galois and the Galois group of the special fiber of \(\widehat {\mathcal C} \to {\mathcal C}\) contains no nontrivial normal subgroup. Hence, the special fiber of \(\widehat{\Psi}\) is the Galois closure of the special fiber of \(\Psi\), as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Spreading out (Poonen, EGA IV) gives smooth proper flat models; enlarge T so the ramification loci are étale; decomposition groups give the Galois closure statement.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: Hilbert's irreducibility theorem implies that we can take $t'\in{\mathbb P}^1(k)$ such that $C_{t'}$ is irreducible. Set \(L := {\mathbf k}(C_{t'})\), set \(\widehat{L}\) to be the Galois closure of \(L/k\), and set \(G := \mathrm{Gal}(\widehat{L}/k)\).  Fix generators \(g_1, \dots, g_r\in G\). By the Chebotarev density theorem, there are places \(v_1, \dots, v_r\in \Omega_k\smallsetminus S\) such that the Frobenius element of \(w_i|v_i\) in $G$ generates the same subgroup as \(g_i\). By Krasner's Lemma, there exists an open neighborhood \(t'\in U_{v_i}\subset {\mathbb P}^1(k_{v_i})\) such that \({\mathbf k}(C_t)\otimes_k k_{v_i} \simeq {\mathbf k}(C_{t'})\otimes_k k_{v_i}\) for all \(t\in U_{v_i}\cap {\mathbb P}^1(k)\)~\cite{PoonenRaPt}*{Prop. 3.5.74}. In particular, since \(g_i\) were chosen to generate \(G\), if \(t\in {\mathbb P}^1(k) \cap \prod_i U_{v_i}\), then \({\mathbf k}(C_t)\) is a field and the Galois group of its Galois closure contains \(G\). Furthermore, for \(v\in S\), Krasner's Lemma implies that there exists an open neighborhood \(t_v\in U_v\subset {\mathbb P}^1(k_v)\) such that \({\mathbf k}(C_t)\otimes_k k_v \simeq {\mathbf k}(C_{t_v})\) for all \(t\in U_v\cap {\mathbb P}^1(k)\). Then weak approximation allows us to find $t\in{\mathbb P}^1(k)\cap \left(\prod_{v\in S} U_v \times \prod_i U_{v_i} \times \prod_{v\notin S\cup T}{\mathbb P}^1(k_v)\right)$ and thus $C_t$ has the claimed properties.

nodes.name: Uniformity of unramified local splitting via cycle types
nodes.statement:
Let \(C\) be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a number field \(k\), let \(\psi\colon C \to {\mathbb P}^1_k\) be a nonconstant morphism, and let \(B\) denote the branch locus.  Assume that the Galois closure of \(\psi\colon C \to {\mathbb P}^1\) is geometrically integral.
    Then for all nonarchimedean \(v\in \Omega_k\) with sufficiently large residue field, the isomorphism types of unramified residue fields is completely determined by the Galois group \(G\) of the Galois closure of \(\psi\).  More precisely, there is a bijection 
    \begin{align*}
       \left\{\mathrm{ct}(g) : g \in G\right\} \quad &\leftrightarrow\quad
        \left\{{\mathbf k}(C_t)\otimes_k k_v : t\in {\mathbb P}^1(k), t\bmod v \notin B({\mathbb F}_v)\right\}/\sim,\\
        (d_i)_{i=1}^r \quad \quad \quad&\mapsto \quad\prod_{i=1}^rk_v(d_i).
        \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For v with large residue field, the unramified local splitting types of fibers are exactly the cycle types of the Galois group of the Galois closure.

nodes.name: Remarks on Theorem 5.3
nodes.statement:
\hfill
\begin{enumerate}
    \item This theorem is essentially~\cite{DG2012}*{Theorem 1.2} combined with Proposition~\ref{prop:etalealg-nonGal}. However, as the proof is fairly short given everything we have proved thus far and citing~\cite{DG2012}*{Theorem 1.2} directly would require verifying that our assumptions imply their assumptions, we elect to give a direct proof.
    \item If the Galois closure of \(\psi\colon C \to {\mathbb P}^1_k\) gives a smooth projective curve \(\widehat{C}\) that is not geometrically integral, then \(\widehat{C}_{k_v}\) may be reducible and the Galois closure of \(\psi\colon C_{k_v} \to {\mathbb P}^1_{k_v}\) may be a proper subcover of \(\widehat{C}_{k_v}\). In this case, one must instead consider the Galois group of the special fiber. Since \(\overline{k}\cap {\mathbf k}(\widehat{C})\) is a finite extension of \(k\), there are only finitely many possibilities for the Galois group of the special fiber, and one can use the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:ChebotarevMain} for each of these possibilities to obtain an analogous result.
    \item The required lower bound on the size of the residue field comes from the effective Chebotarev Density Theorem (see Proposition~\ref{prop:EffCheb}\eqref{part:EffCheb}). As such, it can be made effective, and the explicit bound can be deduced from the proof. 
    \item The bijection in the theorem can be used both ways. nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3
nodes.statement:
Let \(\widehat \psi\colon \widehat C\to {\mathbb P}^1\) be the Galois closure of \(\psi\) and let \(G=\mathrm{Gal}(\widehat{C}/{\mathbb P}^1) < S_d\).
