Furthermore, \(G\) must contain the geometric Galois group of \(G\) must also be \(S_d\). In particular, \(\widehat{C}\) is geometrically integral, and therefore \eqref{part:InertiaSd} follows by Theorem~\ref{thm:ChebotarevMain}.

    By Lemma~\ref{lem:GoodReduction}, there exists a finite set of places \(T\subset \Omega_k\) such that for all nonarchimedean \(v\notin T\), the morphisms \(C\to {\mathbb P}^1_k\) and \(\widehat{C}\to {\mathbb P}^1_k\) have good reduction. Every nonarchimedean place with sufficiently large residue field is outside \(T\), thus we may assume that \(\psi\) has good reduction at \(v\). Let $\Psi\colon {\mathcal C} \to {\mathbb P}^1_{{\mathcal O}_v}$ be an integral model as in Definition~\ref{def:GoodReductionOfCurves}.


    \textbf{\eqref{part:RamificationUpperBoundSd}} Let \(t\in {\mathbb P}^1(k)\) be such that \({\mathbf k}(C_t)\) is ramified at \(v\), and let \(\overline{t}\in {\mathbb P}^1({\mathbb F}_v)\) be the specialization of \(t_v\). Then by Theorem~\ref{thm:RamAndInertiaDegrees}, any maximal subfield \(L\) of \({\mathbf k}({\mathcal C}_{t_v})\) has ramification degree at most \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\) for some \(\overline{x}\in {\mathcal C}_{\overline{t}}\). By assumption, \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t}) \leq 2\), so \(e(L/k_v)\leq 2\) for all maximal subfields \(L\subset {\mathbf k}(C_t)\otimes_k k_v\). 
    It remains to show that the number of ramified places is bounded above by 
        \[
            \max\left\{ \#\{x \in C_t : e(x/t) > 1\} : t\in {\mathbb P}^1(k_v)\ \mbox{a branch point}\right\}.
        \]
Recall that the \'etale algebra \({\mathbf k}(C_t)\otimes_k k_v\) decomposes as a product:
    \[
    {\mathbf k}(C_t)\otimes_k k_v= {\mathbf k}({\mathcal C}_{t_v})=\prod_{\overline{x}\in {\mathcal C}_{\overline{t}}} {\mathbf k}({\mathcal C}_{t_v})_{\overline{x}}, \quad\textup{where}\quad {\mathbf k}({\mathcal C}_{t_v})_{\overline{x}} := \prod_{\substack{x\in ({\mathcal C}_{t_v})_{k_v}\\x\rightsquigarrow \overline{x}}}{\mathbf k}(x).
    \]
    Theorem~\ref{thm:RamAndInertiaDegrees}\eqref{part:Ramification} says that any maximal subfield \(L\) of \({\mathbf k}({\mathcal C}_{t_v})_{\overline{x}}\) has ramification index bounded by \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\), and furthermore if the ramification index of \(L/k_v\) is equal to \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\), then \(L = {\mathbf k}({\mathcal C}_{t_v})_{\overline{x}}\). The assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:SdIntro} imply that \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t})\leq 2\). Thus if \(w|v\) is ramified in \({\mathbf k}(C_t)\) then \({\mathbf k}(C_t)_w \simeq {\mathbf k}({\mathcal C}_{t_v})_{\overline{x}}\) for a unique \(\overline{x}\) with \(e(\overline{x}/\overline{t}) = 2\).
    
    \textbf{\eqref{part:RamificationExistenceSd}} Assume that \(\psi\) has a \(k_v\)-rational branch point \(t_v\in {\mathbb P}^1(k_v)\), that there exists an odd degree ramification point \(x_v\in C\) lying above \(t_v\), and let \(L/{\mathbf k}(x_v)\) be a quadratic ramified extension. By the assumptions on \(\psi\), \(e(x_v/t_v)=2\) and since \(\psi\) has good reduction the same is true for the ramification index and degree of the specializations \(\overline{x},\overline{t}\) of \(x_v, t_v\), respectively. Thus Lemma~\ref{lem:HilbertIrred} applied to \(S = \{v\}\) gives the desired result.
    \qed

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.5
nodes.statement:
We prove by induction on $d$. The case when $d=1$ is trivial.
        Let $H$ be a transitive subgroup of $S_d$ generated by transpositions. Let $a,b \in \{1, \ldots, d-1\}$. Because $H$ is transitive and generated by transpositions, $H$ contains a sequence of transpositions $(a,i_1), (i_1, i_2), \ldots, (i_{n-1}, b)$, and hence we have $(a,b)\in H$. So $\mathrm{Stab}_H(d)$ is generated by transpositions of the set $\{1, \ldots, d-1\}$ by our assumption, and acts transitively on \(\{1,..., d-1\}\). Thus, by the induction hypothesis, $\mathrm{Stab}_H(d) = \mathrm{Stab}_{S_d}(d)\simeq S_{d-1}$. Then we have $H=S_d$, since $H$ must contain a transposition moving $d$.

nodes.statement:
For any positive integer \(m\), the map
            \[
                \{x \in {\mathbb P}^1({\mathbb Q}) : H(x) \leq N\} \to {\mathbb P}^1({\mathbb Z}/m{\mathbb Z})
            \]
            is surjective if \(N\geq \max\left\{\lfloor\sqrt{m}\rfloor,\ \frac{m}{\min\{p\text{ prime}\,:\,p\mid m\}}\right\}\) and injective if \(N<\sqrt{m/2}\).  Moreover, these bounds are sharp: 
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item If \(p = n^2 + 1\) is prime, then \([n:1]\in {\mathbb P}^1({\mathbb F}_p)\) is not the image of any point \(x\in {\mathbb P}^1({\mathbb Q})\) with \(H(x) < n = \lfloor \sqrt{p}\rfloor\). \item If \(m = 2m_0\), then \([m_0 : 1]\in {\mathbb P}^1({\mathbb Z}/m{\mathbb Z})\) is not the image of any point \(x\in {\mathbb P}^1({\mathbb Q})\) with \(H(x) < m_0 = \frac{m}{2}\). \item If \(p = (n-1)^2 + n^2\) is prime, then \(x := [n:1-n]\) and \(x' := [n-1:n]\) have height \(n = \lceil\sqrt{p/2}\rceil\) and \(x\equiv x'\bmod p\). \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.7
nodes.statement:
We follow the standard argument of counting points of bounded height, first written out by Schanuel, while keeping track of the modulo \(m\) images.
        
        We would like to estimate
        \[F(N)=\#\{(a,b)\in{\mathbb Z}^2: b\geq 1,\ a\neq 0,\ \max\{|a|,|b|\}\leq N,\ \gcd(a,b)=1,\ [a:b]\bmod m={[u:v]}\}.\]
        The only points that have been dropped from  ${\mathbb P}^1({\mathbb Q})$ are $[0:1]$ and $[1:0]$, which are finitely many points. 
        
        We first allow $\gcd(a,b)\geq 1$ but assume that $\gcd(a,b,m)=1$, and will fix this discrepancy later.
        The condition $[a:b]\equiv [u:v]\bmod m$ is equivalent to $a\equiv ug\bmod m$ and $b\equiv vg\bmod m$ for some integer $g\in({\mathbb Z}/m{\mathbb Z})^\times$. There are precisely $\varphi(m)=\#({\mathbb Z}/m{\mathbb Z})^\times$ many choices of  $g\in({\mathbb Z}/m{\mathbb Z})^\times$ satisfying the equations because \(u,v\) generate \({\mathbb Z}/m{\mathbb Z}\).
        We cut up the box defined by $1\leq b\leq N$ and $1\leq |a|\leq N$ into $m\times m$ boxes, we have
        \[\#\{(a,b)\in{\mathbb Z}^2:1\leq |a|, b\leq N,
        \ \gcd(a,b,m)=1,\ [a:b]\equiv {[u:v]}\bmod m\}
                =\varphi(m)\frac{2N^2}{m^2}+O(N).
        \]
        
        To impose the $\gcd(a,b)=1$ condition, we will carry out M\"obius inversion.
        Suppose $A\mid \gcd(a,b)$, then we can take a factor of $A$ out of both $a$ and $b$, and the new $a,b$ runs up to $N/A$. Therefore we deduce that
        \[S(N,A){\colonequals}\sum_{1\leq b\leq N}\sum_{\substack{1\leq |a|\leq N\\  [a:b]\equiv [u:v]\bmod m\\ \gcd(a,b,m)=1\\ A\mid \gcd(a,b)}}1
        =\varphi(m)\frac{2N^2}{A^2m^2}+O\left(\frac{N}{A}\right).\]
        M\"obius inversion formula gives
        \[F(N)=\sum_{\substack{A\leq N\\\gcd(A,m)=1}} \mu(A)S(N,A)
            =\left(\frac{2N^2\varphi(m)}{m^2}\sum_{\substack{A\leq N\\\gcd(A,m)=1}}\frac{\mu(A)}{A^2}\right)+O\left(N\log N\right)
            .\]
        If we extend the inner sum to all positive integers $A$, we have 
        \[\sum_{\substack{A\\\gcd(A,m)=1}}\frac{\mu(A)}{A^2}
        =\prod_{p\nmid m}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^2}\right)
        =\frac{1}{\zeta(2)}\prod_{p\mid m}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^2}\right)^{-1}
        =\frac{6}{\pi^2}\prod_{p\mid m}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^2}\right)^{-1}.
        \]
        Truncating the infinite sum, we have
        \[\sum_{\substack{A\leq N\\\gcd(A,m)=1}}\frac{\mu(A)}{A^2}=\sum_{\substack{A\\\gcd(A,m)=1}}\frac{\mu(A)}{A^2}+O\left(\sum_{A> N}\frac{1}{A^2}\right)
        =\frac{6}{\pi^2}\prod_{p\mid m}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^2}\right)^{-1}+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right).
        \]
        Therefore
        \[F(N)=\frac{12N^2\varphi(m)}{\pi^2 m^2}\prod_{p\mid m}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^2}\right)^{-1}+O\left(N\log N\right)
            = \frac{12N^2}{\pi^2 m}\prod_{i=1}^r\left(1+\frac{1}{p_i}\right)^{-1}+O\left(N\log N\right)\]
        as required.
nodes.statement_short: Schanuel-style counting: count lattice points in residue classes box by box, then impose coprimality by Möbius inversion.

            =\left(\frac{2N^2\varphi(m)}{m^2}\sum_{\substack{A\leq N\\\gcd(A,m)=1}}\frac{\mu(A)}{A^2}\right)+O\left(N\log N\right)
            .\]
nodes.statement_short: Möbius inversion.

nodes.name: Evaluate the Euler product and truncation error
nodes.statement:
If we extend the inner sum to all positive integers $A$, we have 
        \[\sum_{\substack{A\\\gcd(A,m)=1}}\frac{\mu(A)}{A^2}
        =\prod_{p\nmid m}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^2}\right)
        =\frac{1}{\zeta(2)}\prod_{p\mid m}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^2}\right)^{-1}
        =\frac{6}{\pi^2}\prod_{p\mid m}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^2}\right)^{-1}.
        \]
        Truncating the infinite sum, we have
        \[\sum_{\substack{A\leq N\\\gcd(A,m)=1}}\frac{\mu(A)}{A^2}=\sum_{\substack{A\\\gcd(A,m)=1}}\frac{\mu(A)}{A^2}+O\left(\sum_{A> N}\frac{1}{A^2}\right)
        =\frac{6}{\pi^2}\prod_{p\mid m}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^2}\right)^{-1}+O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right).
        \]
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the Euler product and truncation error.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement:
Therefore
        \[F(N)=\frac{12N^2\varphi(m)}{\pi^2 m^2}\prod_{p\mid m}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^2}\right)^{-1}+O\left(N\log N\right)
            = \frac{12N^2}{\pi^2 m}\prod_{i=1}^r\left(1+\frac{1}{p_i}\right)^{-1}+O\left(N\log N\right)\]
        as required.
nodes.statement_short: Combine.
